questions.stem: A public health officer notes that in a malaria-endemic district, severe disease is concentrated in young children while local adults usually have mild illness. Travelers to the district are also at high risk. Which of the following best explains this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children clear hypnozoites from the liver more slowly than adults do

choices.label: B
choices.text: Children do not express the Duffy antigen until later in childhood

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children have more fetal hemoglobin, which favors parasite replication

choices.label: D
choices.text: Children have not yet acquired the partial immunity common in local adults

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mosquitoes preferentially bite children, delivering a larger parasite inoculum

explanation.summary: Children in endemic areas, like travelers, lack the partial immunity that repeated exposure gives local adults.
explanation.whyCorrect: In areas where malaria is endemic, children are the group most susceptible to the disease because they have not yet acquired the partial immunity that is common in adults in those regions. People who travel to areas of endemicity are at high risk for the same reason. The majority of malaria deaths occur in children younger than 5 years of age.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hypnozoites cause relapse in P. vivax and P. ovale infection and are not described as differing by age.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Absence of the Duffy antigen is an inherited trait that protects against P. vivax; it is not an age-dependent change.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fetal hemoglobin favoring parasite growth is not among the described host factors; the abnormal hemoglobins discussed are protective.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Differential biting of children is not the stated reason for their susceptibility.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A ministry of health is designing a program to reduce malaria transmission in a rural endemic district. Which of the following combinations of measures has shown success in preventing malaria?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gloves, masks, and eye protection during veterinary procedures

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mosquito netting, insecticides, and seasonal chemoprophylaxis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pasteurization of dairy products and vaccination of livestock

choices.label: D
choices.text: Removal of attached ticks within 36 hours and avoidance of leaf litter

choices.label: E
choices.text: Screening of blood donors for absence of the Duffy antigen

explanation.summary: Malaria prevention relies on mosquito netting, insecticides, and seasonal chemoprophylaxis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mosquito netting, insecticides, and seasonal chemoprophylaxis (using drugs to prevent disease) have shown some success in malaria prevention. The RTS,S vaccine is an additional measure recommended for young children in areas endemic for P. falciparum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Personal protective equipment during veterinary procedures prevents brucellosis in people who work around unvaccinated animals.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pasteurization and livestock vaccination prevent brucellosis, which is common in countries that do not vaccinate livestock.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prompt tick removal is the prevention strategy for babesiosis, transmitted by Ixodes scapularis, not for malaria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Absence of the Duffy antigen is a protective host trait, not a donor screening strategy for preventing malaria.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A Giemsa-stained blood smear from a patient with heavy Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia shows abundant ring forms but essentially no mature trophozoites or schizonts. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mature forms are rapidly phagocytosed by macrophages in the spleen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mature forms convert into crescent-shaped gametocytes before they can be seen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mature forms lose their affinity for the Giemsa stain used on the smear

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mature forms return to the liver to complete their development

choices.label: E
choices.text: RBCs carrying mature forms express PfEMP1 and bind small-vessel endothelium

explanation.summary: P. falciparum-infected RBCs bearing mature forms express PfEMP1 and sequester on small-vessel endothelium, so they are rarely seen in peripheral blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although all RBC stages of Plasmodium can be seen in blood smears, the most common form is the ring form of the trophozoite, which occurs early in maturation. It is particularly uncommon to see mature trophozoites or schizonts of P. falciparum because RBCs carrying these forms express adhesion molecules like PfEMP1 that bind to the endothelial lining of small blood vessels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Splenic clearance of mature forms is not the described reason they are absent from the smear; they are sequestered on endothelium.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Only some parasites commit to gametocytes; the absence of mature asexual forms is explained by endothelial binding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Giemsa staining reveals all RBC stages of the parasite; the issue is that mature forms are not circulating.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Once merozoites leave the liver, the parasite continues in the erythrocytic cycle and does not return to hepatocytes.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A clinic in a remote area has no reliable electricity, no refrigeration, and no trained microscopist. A febrile patient is suspected of having malaria. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic test in this setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A rapid diagnostic test employing specific monoclonal antibodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood culture incubated and held for up to 7 days in the laboratory

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measurement of serum lactate dehydrogenase and haptoglobin levels

choices.label: D
choices.text: Paired acute and convalescent serology drawn more than 2 weeks apart

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thick and thin Giemsa-stained blood smears read on site

explanation.summary: Rapid antigen tests using monoclonal antibodies need no electricity or refrigeration, making them suited to resource-limited settings.
explanation.whyCorrect: When microscopy is not available, rapid diagnostic tests for malaria may be used. These rapid tests employ specific monoclonal antibodies, and because they do not require electricity or refrigeration, they are increasingly used in areas with limited medical resources.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood culture is the approach used for brucellosis and requires laboratory infrastructure unavailable here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LDH and haptoglobin reflect hemolysis generally and do not establish the presence or species of the parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Paired serology is used for brucellosis and requires a second sample more than 2 weeks later, delaying treatment of an acute febrile illness.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Giemsa-stained microscopy is the gold standard but is explicitly unavailable, since the clinic has no microscopist.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A parasitologist is describing the natural life cycle of Babesia microti in the northeastern United States. Which of the following animals serves as the reservoir for this organism?

explanation.summary: The white-footed mouse is the reservoir for B. microti, while the Ixodes tick is the definitive host.
explanation.whyCorrect: The life cycle of Babesia microti involves two main hosts: the white-footed mouse (Peromyscus leucopus), which serves as the reservoir, and the Ixodes tick, which is the definitive host in which the gametes unite and undergo sexual reproduction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cattle are the animal host for Brucella abortus, not a reservoir for Babesia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Humans are accidental, dead-end hosts and do not continue the natural cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Anopheles mosquito is the vector for Plasmodium spp.; Babesia is transmitted by the Ixodes tick.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Although Ixodes scapularis is called the deer tick, the reservoir named for B. microti is the white-footed mouse.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman acquires babesiosis after an Ixodes bite in Rhode Island. Which of the following best describes what the parasite does in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Male and female gametes unite in the blood, forming new sporozoites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Merozoites stay dormant in the liver and reactivate years later

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sporozoites invade hepatocytes and form schizonts before entering RBCs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sporozoites invade RBCs and reproduce asexually, and the human is a dead-end host

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism survives and replicates inside macrophages of the reticuloendothelial system

explanation.summary: In humans, Babesia sporozoites invade RBCs and reproduce asexually, causing hemolysis, and the human is an accidental dead-end host.
explanation.whyCorrect: Humans become accidental, dead-end hosts when bitten by an infected tick. In humans, sporozoites invade red blood cells and reproduce asexually, leading to hemolysis and clinical symptoms such as fever, anemia, and fatigue. Humans do not continue the natural cycle, although human-to-human transmission can occur through blood transfusion and, rarely, congenitally.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gametes unite and undergo sexual reproduction inside the tick, the definitive host, not in human blood.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dormant liver forms that reactivate years later are hypnozoites of P. vivax and P. ovale.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A hepatocyte schizont stage before RBC invasion is part of the Plasmodium life cycle, not the Babesia life cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Replication inside macrophages with spread through the reticuloendothelial system describes Brucella spp.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A hiker in Massachusetts finds a tiny nymphal tick attached to her leg after an afternoon outdoors and asks whether removing it right away matters. Which of the following is the most accurate statement about transmission of Babesia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Transmission depends only on the tick species and not on attachment time

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transmission occurs only from adult ticks, so nymphal ticks carry no risk

choices.label: C
choices.text: Transmission occurs within minutes of attachment, so prompt removal does not help

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transmission requires the tick to feed to full engorgement over about 7 days

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transmission takes 36-72 hours after attachment, so prompt removal prevents infection

explanation.summary: Babesia transmission takes 36-72 hours after tick attachment, so ticks should be removed as soon as possible.
explanation.whyCorrect: Like Lyme disease and Rocky Mountain spotted fever, transmission of the pathogen is not instant but takes 36-72 hours after attachment of I. scapularis. Any ticks should be removed as soon as possible to prevent infection, but young ticks (nymphs) can be hard to spot, so a thorough check after being outdoors is needed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Attachment time is central to transmission risk, which is the basis for prompt tick removal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nymphs do transmit infection and are in fact the harder stage to detect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Transmission is explicitly not instant, which is why prompt removal is effective.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Full engorgement over 7 days is not the stated requirement; the window is 36-72 hours.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man in northern California develops fever and hemolytic anemia, and a blood smear shows intraerythrocytic parasites. He has not traveled outside the state. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: B. duncani causes the small number of babesiosis cases seen on the west coast of the United States.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the US, B. microti causes most cases of babesiosis in the northeastern US, but other species can cause disease to a lesser extent. B. duncani causes a small number of cases on the west coast of the US, which fits a patient who acquired intraerythrocytic infection in northern California.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anaplasma phagocytophilum shares the Ixodes vector but is not one of the intraerythrocytic parasites seen inside RBCs on smear.
whyWrongByChoice.C: B. microti accounts for most cases in the northeastern US rather than on the west coast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Borrelia burgdorferi causes Lyme disease and does not appear as a parasite within red blood cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: P. knowlesi is a primate malaria parasite responsible for a small number of human cases and would require exposure in an endemic region abroad.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A febrile, anemic patient with a recent Ixodes bite has a Giemsa-stained smear showing intraerythrocytic parasites, but no tetrads are seen and the forms could also be consistent with Plasmodium. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin empiric treatment directed at cerebral malaria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Obtain blood cultures for small gram-negative coccobacilli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeat the blood smear daily until tetrads appear

choices.label: D
choices.text: Send PCR and paired serology to distinguish the two parasites

choices.label: E
choices.text: Test the patient's red blood cells for absence of the Duffy antigen

explanation.summary: When the Maltese cross is absent and the smear is inconclusive, PCR and paired serology distinguish Babesia from Plasmodium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Maltese cross will not always be present in a blood smear in babesiosis patients. In those instances, distinguishing between Babesia and Plasmodium spp. may be difficult and requires other laboratory techniques, such as PCR or serology. These are usually employed only when the blood smear is inconclusive and another similar parasite is suspected.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Empiric treatment for cerebral malaria does not resolve the diagnostic question and does not fit a patient with local tick exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood cultures for gram-negative coccobacilli are used to diagnose brucellosis, not an intraerythrocytic parasite.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Waiting for tetrads is unreliable because the Maltese cross may never appear on the smear.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Duffy antigen status relates to susceptibility to P. vivax and does not identify the organism on this smear.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old pig farmer develops brucellosis. Which of the following species is the most likely cause of his infection?

explanation.summary: Brucella suis is the species associated with pigs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Four major species of Brucella are responsible for human disease, each linked to a particular animal host: B. melitensis in goats and sheep, B. abortus in cattle, B. suis in pigs, and B. canis in dogs. A pig farmer is therefore most likely infected with B. suis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Babesia microti is a tick-borne protozoan that infects RBCs and is not a cause of brucellosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: B. abortus is the species associated with cattle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: B. canis is associated with dogs and is the less common of the four major species.
whyWrongByChoice.D: B. melitensis is associated with goats and sheep; it is the most virulent and most common cause worldwide but does not fit swine exposure.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: Brucella organisms ingested in unpasteurized cheese must survive the stomach and intestine before reaching host tissue. Which of the following pairs of adaptations allows them to do so?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acid-fast mycolic acids and an efflux pump that expels bile salts

choices.label: B
choices.text: Flagella for motility and an exotoxin that lyses intestinal enterocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spore formation in the stomach and germination within the distal ileum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Superoxide dismutase that buffers gastric acid and a capsule that repels bile salts

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urease that neutralizes gastric acid and cholyglycine hydrolase that hydrolyzes bile salts

explanation.summary: Brucella secretes urease to neutralize stomach acid and cholyglycine hydrolase to hydrolyze intestinal bile salts, then crosses M cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Brucella spp. have several adaptations that allow them to survive the gastrointestinal immune system. They secrete urease, which neutralizes the acidity of the stomach. B. abortus, B. melitensis, and B. suis synthesize an enzyme that hydrolyzes intestinal bile salts, called cholyglycine hydrolase. They can then cross M cells to enter through the intestinal epithelium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acid-fast mycolic acids are a mycobacterial feature and are not how Brucella survives passage through the gut.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Flagellar motility and an enterocyte-lysing exotoxin are not among the described adaptations of Brucella.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Brucella spp. are gram-negative coccobacilli and are not described as spore formers.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Superoxide dismutase is secreted to counteract the oxidative burst inside phagocytes, not to buffer stomach acid.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A phagocyte engulfs Brucella and mounts an oxidative burst, yet the bacterium survives inside the cell. Which of the following best accounts for this survival?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It coats itself in host immunoglobulin to avoid immune recognition

choices.label: B
choices.text: It escapes the phagosome into the cytosol using a pore-forming hemolysin

choices.label: C
choices.text: It prevents fusion of the phagosome with the cell nucleus

choices.label: D
choices.text: It secretes superoxide dismutase, which neutralizes reactive oxygen species

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its lipopolysaccharide binds and inactivates complement component C3b

explanation.summary: Phagocytosed Brucella secrete superoxide dismutase to counteract the phagocyte's oxidative burst.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once in the tissues, the LPS of Brucella spp. is not well recognized by pattern recognition receptors, allowing the bacteria to colonize without inducing strong phagocyte activation. If phagocytosed, Brucella spp. secrete superoxide dismutase to counteract the oxidative burst, which is why the bacteria escape destruction and go on to survive and replicate inside macrophages.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coating in host immunoglobulin is not among the described immune evasion strategies of Brucella.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Brucella survives and replicates within the macrophage rather than escaping into the cytosol through a hemolysin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Phagosomes fuse with lysosomes, not with the nucleus, so this is not a coherent evasion mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The relevant property of Brucella LPS is that it is poorly recognized by pattern recognition receptors, not that it inactivates C3b.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A veterinarian is instructed to wear gloves, a mask, and eye protection when assisting the delivery of a calf from an unvaccinated cow, and to treat the placenta as highly infectious. Which of the following best explains why placental and reproductive tissues carry the greatest risk of transmitting Brucella?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amniotic fluid inactivates the disinfectants used in veterinary practice

choices.label: B
choices.text: Brucella forms heat-resistant spores within uterine tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Brucella is shed only at parturition and at no other time

choices.label: D
choices.text: Erythritol in these tissues promotes growth of Brucella to high concentrations

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fetal blood carries the receptor Brucella uses to enter macrophages

explanation.summary: Erythritol, abundant in ruminant placenta and reproductive tissue, promotes Brucella growth, making those tissues highly infectious.
explanation.whyCorrect: Brucella spp. are highly concentrated in the placenta and reproductive tissues of infected animals, especially when the animal is pregnant. Erythritol, a sugar alcohol found in high amounts in the placenta, mammary glands, and reproductive tract of ruminants, promotes the growth of Brucella. Brucella can cause miscarriages in infected animals, and discarded placental tissue is highly infectious.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inactivation of disinfectants by amniotic fluid is not a described reason for the risk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Brucella spp. are gram-negative coccobacilli and are not described as forming spores.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Transmission also occurs through direct contact with infected animals, unpasteurized dairy, and inhalation, so shedding is not confined to parturition.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The hazard is the high bacterial load promoted by erythritol, not a receptor carried in fetal blood.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man has had 5 weeks of intermittent fever, night sweats with a characteristic wet hay odor, low back pain, and weight loss. Brucellosis is suspected, but organisms are not seen on stained preparations of his blood. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to establish the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A rapid antigen test employing specific monoclonal antibodies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood culture plus paired titers showing a four-fold rise

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bone marrow biopsy examined for intraerythrocytic tetrads

choices.label: D
choices.text: Measurement of serum lactate dehydrogenase and haptoglobin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat staining of a thick blood film with Giemsa

explanation.summary: Brucellosis is diagnosed by culture or a four-fold or greater rise in antibody titers drawn more than 2 weeks apart.
explanation.whyCorrect: Visualization of Brucella spp. is very difficult, and the low levels of bacteria make staining a poor way to diagnose brucellosis. Diagnosis is most commonly made either by culture of the organism or by a four-fold or greater rise in Brucella antibody titers more than 2 weeks apart. A total antibody titer of 1:160 or greater, or a positive PCR, is sufficient for a presumptive diagnosis pending culture and convalescent phase serum results.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rapid monoclonal antibody tests are the fallback for diagnosing malaria where microscopy is unavailable.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intraerythrocytic tetrads are the Maltese cross forms of Babesia and would not be sought to diagnose brucellosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LDH and haptoglobin reflect hemolysis, which is a feature of malaria and babesiosis rather than brucellosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Repeating the stain will not help, because low bacterial levels make staining an unreliable way to diagnose brucellosis.

questions.topicName: Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man plans a 2-week humanitarian trip to rural Kenya, a region with known chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum. He tells you he would prefer a prophylactic regimen that he can stop as soon as possible after returning home. Which of the following is the most appropriate chemoprophylaxis?

explanation.summary: Atovaquone-proguanil is a preferred prophylactic for chloroquine-resistant regions and has the shortest post-travel course.
explanation.whyCorrect: Atovaquone-proguanil is effective in chloroquine-resistant areas and is often the first choice for travelers. It is started 1-2 days before exposure and continued only 7 days after leaving the area, the shortest post-travel course among the options, and is generally well tolerated.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloroquine is ineffective in chloroquine-resistant regions such as East Africa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is effective for prophylaxis but must be continued for 4 weeks after travel, a much longer post-travel course.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mefloquine must be continued 4 weeks after travel and carries a black box warning for neuropsychiatric effects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primaquine is less commonly used for prophylaxis and has activity primarily against P. ovale and P. vivax, not falciparum.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A patient with malaria is treated with chloroquine, which accumulates in the parasite's digestive vacuole. Which of the following best describes how this drug kills Plasmodium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It binds parasite DNA and disrupts mitochondria

choices.label: B
choices.text: It forms free radicals after cleavage by heme iron

choices.label: D
choices.text: It inhibits protein synthesis at the 30S ribosomal subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: It prevents conversion of toxic heme to hemozoin

explanation.summary: Chloroquine interferes with digestive vacuole function, allowing toxic heme to accumulate.
explanation.whyCorrect: In red blood cells the parasite feeds on hemoglobin and must convert heme to hemozoin because heme is toxic to it. Chloroquine increases vacuole pH and interferes with lysosomal degradation of hemoglobin, so toxic heme accumulates and damages the parasite's membranes, leading to death.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Binding parasite DNA and disrupting mitochondria describes primaquine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Free-radical formation after cleavage by heme iron describes the artemisinins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibition of mitochondrial electron transport is the mechanism of atovaquone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibition of the 30S ribosomal subunit is the mechanism of doxycycline.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is diagnosed with Plasmodium vivax malaria. Before prescribing an agent to prevent relapse, the physician orders glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) testing. Concern about hemolysis from which of the following drugs prompted this test?

explanation.summary: Primaquine carries a risk of hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primaquine is used against the exoerythrocytic stages of P. ovale and P. vivax to prevent relapse, but it carries a risk of causing hemolytic anemia in patients with G6PD deficiency, so G6PD status should be checked first.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Artemether acts via free-radical generation and is not associated with G6PD hemolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Atovaquone-proguanil is eliminated by the kidneys and is contraindicated in severe renal failure, not associated with G6PD hemolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline causes GI disturbances and photosensitivity, not G6PD-related hemolysis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mefloquine's main concern is neuropsychiatric effects, not hemolysis.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A patient has recovered from an acute episode of Plasmodium ovale malaria but remains at risk of relapse from dormant liver forms. Which of the following drugs is most appropriate to target the exoerythrocytic stage and prevent relapse?

explanation.summary: Primaquine is used to prevent relapse of P. ovale and P. vivax.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primaquine disrupts mitochondria and binds to DNA within the parasite, making it effective against the exoerythrocytic (liver) stages. Its best and most common use is preventing relapses of P. ovale and P. vivax.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Artesunate targets acute blood-stage parasites in severe malaria, not dormant liver forms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Azithromycin is used for babesiosis, not for malaria relapse prevention.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chloroquine acts on blood-stage parasites in the digestive vacuole and does not clear dormant liver forms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline inhibits protein synthesis and is not the agent used to prevent relapse from liver stages.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman with a history of major depression and a seizure disorder requests malaria prophylaxis before travel. Because of a black box warning for neuropsychiatric disorders, which of the following drugs should be avoided?

explanation.summary: Mefloquine is contraindicated in patients with psychiatric disorders or seizures.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mefloquine carries a black box warning for neuropsychiatric disorders and is contraindicated in patients with major psychiatric disorders or a history of seizures. It can also cause abnormal dreams and insomnia that often limit its use.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atovaquone-proguanil is generally well tolerated, with mainly GI effects and a caution in renal impairment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloroquine's main concerns are pruritus, cardiac effects, and hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline's main concerns are GI upset and photosensitivity, not neuropsychiatric effects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primaquine's concerns are QT prolongation, leukopenia, and hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A traveler taking doxycycline for malaria prophylaxis also takes a daily multivitamin containing calcium and iron. His physician warns that this may make the doxycycline less effective. Which of the following best explains this interaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cations chelate doxycycline, reducing its absorption

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cations compete with doxycycline at the 80S ribosome

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cations increase renal clearance of the drug

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cations induce CYP3A4 and accelerate drug metabolism

choices.label: E
choices.text: The cations trigger hemolysis of red blood cells

explanation.summary: Doxycycline is chelated by cations, which makes it less effective.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline is contraindicated when given with cations because chelation occurs, and this renders the drug less effective. Cations such as calcium, magnesium, and iron are commonly found in multivitamins.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxycycline inhibits the 30S subunit; the cation interaction is chelation, not ribosomal competition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The reduced efficacy is due to chelation and impaired absorption, not increased renal clearance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The interaction is chelation in the gut, not CYP3A4 induction; CYP3A4 is relevant to azithromycin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hemolysis is a concern with primaquine or chloroquine in G6PD deficiency, not a cation interaction.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman returns from sub-Saharan Africa with fever and is diagnosed with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria (parasitemia 2%, no organ dysfunction) acquired in a chloroquine-resistant region. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line therapy?

explanation.summary: ACT is first-line for uncomplicated malaria in chloroquine-resistant areas.
explanation.whyCorrect: Given the rate of resistance in most areas, first-line therapy for uncomplicated malaria is artemisinin combination therapy. ACT is preferred because of its low adverse effect profile, over 95% cure rate, and the most rapid clearance of the parasite.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloroquine is preferred only in regions without chloroquine resistance, not in a resistant region.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hydroxychloroquine works the same as chloroquine and is ineffective in a chloroquine-resistant region.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline is slow-acting and used as an alternative or adjunct, not as first-line monotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primaquine monotherapy is used to prevent relapse of P. ovale and P. vivax, not as first-line treatment of falciparum.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A patient with Plasmodium falciparum malaria has a parasitemia of 8%, jaundice, metabolic acidosis, and altered mental status. Which of the following is the preferred initial therapy?

explanation.summary: IV artesunate is the preferred therapy for severe (complicated) malaria.
explanation.whyCorrect: This presentation, with parasitemia over 4% and organ dysfunction, is complicated malaria. Intravenous artesunate is the preferred therapy for severe malaria; IV medication is initiated for at least 24 hours, after which the patient can take oral medication.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Oral atovaquone-proguanil is only a bridge if IV artesunate is not readily available, not the preferred initial therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oral chloroquine is inadequate for severe malaria and would be ineffective if resistance is present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline should be avoided in severe malaria because it is slow-acting relative to other agents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primaquine targets liver-stage relapse and is not used for acute severe blood-stage falciparum.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: Artemether and artesunate are metabolized to dihydroartemisinin, which is activated within the infected red blood cell. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which this active metabolite kills Plasmodium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Binding parasite DNA to block relapse

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cleavage of an endoperoxide bridge by iron

choices.label: E
choices.text: Raising the pH of the digestive vacuole

explanation.summary: Artemisinins are activated by heme iron and generate damaging free radicals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dihydroartemisinin is activated by heme iron binding: the artemisinins cleave the Fe2+ of the endoperoxide bridge and form free radicals. This results in oxidative stress, inhibition of protein and nucleic acid synthesis, ultrastructural changes, and decreased growth and survival of the parasite.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Binding parasite DNA to prevent relapse describes primaquine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase is the action of proguanil.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibition of the 30S subunit is the mechanism of doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Raising vacuole pH describes chloroquine, not the artemisinins.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A patient with HIV is diagnosed with babesiosis. Which of the following is the preferred first-line treatment regimen?

explanation.summary: First-line babesiosis therapy is azithromycin plus atovaquone.
explanation.whyCorrect: The preferred treatment regimen for babesiosis consists of the macrolide azithromycin plus atovaquone, and it is generally well tolerated. Treatment is the same regardless of the patient's immune status.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloroquine is an antimalarial and is not used for babesiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin plus mefloquine (or quinine) is an alternative used only if first-line is contraindicated or not tolerated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Artemether-lumefantrine is an antimalarial ACT regimen, not a treatment for babesiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline plus gentamicin is the first-line regimen for brucellosis, not babesiosis.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A patient with brucellosis is started on doxycycline plus gentamicin. Because of the aminoglycoside component, the physician should monitor for which of the following toxicities?

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides such as gentamicin can cause nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Brucellosis is treated with doxycycline plus an aminoglycoside, usually gentamicin. Aminoglycosides have a number of adverse effects, most importantly nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemolysis in G6PD deficiency is associated with primaquine and chloroquine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Photosensitivity is an adverse effect of doxycycline, not the aminoglycoside.
whyWrongByChoice.D: QT prolongation is associated with azithromycin and primaquine, not aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neuropsychiatric disturbance is associated with mefloquine.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A patient being treated for brucellosis cannot tolerate an aminoglycoside. Doxycycline should instead be combined with which of the following?

explanation.summary: When an aminoglycoside is not tolerated, doxycycline is paired with a fluoroquinolone or SMX-TMP.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the event that a patient cannot tolerate an aminoglycoside, a fluoroquinolone or sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim is used with doxycycline instead for brucellosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Artesunate is used for malaria, not brucellosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Atovaquone is paired with azithromycin for babesiosis, not used for brucellosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chloroquine is an antimalarial and has no role in brucellosis therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primaquine is used to prevent malaria relapse, not to treat brucellosis.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman in the United States is to begin weekly prophylaxis before travel to a region where Plasmodium falciparum has no chloroquine resistance. The pharmacy dispenses hydroxychloroquine rather than chloroquine. Which of the following best describes hydroxychloroquine compared with chloroquine?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It also eradicates the dormant liver forms of Plasmodium vivax and ovale

choices.label: B
choices.text: It can be safely discontinued 7 days after the last malaria exposure

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has a different parasite target in the red cell and must be dosed daily

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a hydroxylated derivative that works the same but is potentially less toxic

choices.label: E
choices.text: It remains effective against chloroquine-resistant strains of Plasmodium falciparum

explanation.summary: Hydroxychloroquine is a chloroquine derivative with an added hydroxyl group; the two drugs work identically.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hydroxychloroquine is more often prescribed in the United States because of its greater availability. It is a derivative of chloroquine with a hydroxyl group added to its structure, which makes it potentially less toxic, but both drugs work the exact same way.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neither drug clears exoerythrocytic liver forms; primaquine is used to prevent relapse of P. vivax and P. ovale.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine must be continued 4 weeks after the last exposure; the 7-day course applies to atovaquone-proguanil and primaquine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both drugs share the same target in the digestive vacuole, and chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine prophylaxis is dosed once weekly, not daily.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hydroxychloroquine works the same as chloroquine and therefore offers no advantage where chloroquine resistance is present.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A rheumatologist prescribes hydroxychloroquine for a 48-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis. Which of the following best explains the antirheumatic effect of this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It blocks conversion of heme to hemozoin within the acidic food vacuole of the parasite

choices.label: B
choices.text: It depletes circulating CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes that infiltrate synovium by triggering apoptosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: It irreversibly acetylates cyclooxygenase-1 in synovial tissue and blocks prostaglandin synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: It neutralizes tumor necrosis factor alpha released by synovial macrophages before it engages its receptor

choices.label: E
choices.text: It raises the pH of acidic compartments and reduces peptide-MHC class II complex formation

explanation.summary: Hydroxychloroquine's antirheumatic action comes from interference with antigen processing in antigen-presenting cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The drug increases pH within intracellular vacuoles and alters protein degradation in the lysosome. Acidic cytoplasmic compartments are required for antigenic protein to be digested and for peptides to assemble with the alpha and beta chains of MHC class II proteins, so antimalarials diminish formation of the peptide-MHC complexes needed to stimulate CD4+ T cells, down-regulating the response to autoantigenic peptides.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blocking heme-to-hemozoin conversion is how the drug kills Plasmodium in erythrocytes, not how it treats autoimmune disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The effect is on antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells rather than depletion of CD8+ cytotoxic lymphocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Irreversible cyclooxygenase inhibition is the action of aspirin, not of hydroxychloroquine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neutralizing tumor necrosis factor alpha is the action of biologic agents; hydroxychloroquine's mechanism is described as unique among autoimmune medications.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with severe renal failure maintained on hemodialysis plans a 10-day trip to a chloroquine-resistant area of East Africa. He departs in 3 days. Which of the following is the most appropriate chemoprophylaxis?

explanation.summary: Severe renal failure rules out atovaquone-proguanil, and a 3-day lead time rules out mefloquine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline is effective in chloroquine-resistant regions, is started only 1-2 days before the first exposure, and has no renal contraindication. It is continued once daily during travel and for 4 weeks after the last exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atovaquone-proguanil is eliminated by the kidneys and is contraindicated in severe renal failure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloroquine is ineffective in a chloroquine-resistant region and must also be started 1-2 weeks before exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hydroxychloroquine works the same as chloroquine and is therefore ineffective where chloroquine resistance exists.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mefloquine is preferably started 3 weeks before the first exposure, which is not possible with a 3-day lead time.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old traveler will take mefloquine once weekly for malaria prophylaxis. How long before the first exposure is it preferable to begin this drug?

explanation.summary: Mefloquine has the longest recommended lead time of the prophylactic antimalarials.
explanation.whyCorrect: The anti-malarial comparison data list mefloquine as once-weekly dosing initiated 3 weeks before the first exposure as the preferable interval, with discontinuation 4 weeks after the last exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: One week is shorter than any listed initiation interval for mefloquine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A 1-2 day lead time applies to atovaquone-proguanil, doxycycline, and primaquine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two weeks is listed only as an acceptable alternative, not the preferable lead time.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Four weeks is the interval for discontinuation after the last exposure, not for initiation.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman is traveling to a Middle Eastern region where Plasmodium falciparum has no chloroquine resistance, and chloroquine is selected for prophylaxis. Which of the following is the correct schedule?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Once daily, begun 1-2 days before exposure and continued 4 weeks after

choices.label: B
choices.text: Once daily, begun 1-2 days before exposure and continued 7 days after

choices.label: C
choices.text: Once weekly, begun 1-2 days before exposure and continued 7 days after

choices.label: D
choices.text: Once weekly, begun 1-2 weeks before exposure and continued 4 weeks after

choices.label: E
choices.text: Once weekly, begun 3 weeks before exposure and continued 4 weeks after

explanation.summary: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine are weekly agents with a 1-2 week lead-in and a 4-week tail.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine is still the preferred therapy in regions that do not have chloroquine resistance. It is dosed once weekly, initiated 1-2 weeks before the first exposure, and discontinued 4 weeks after the last exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Once daily with a 1-2 day lead-in and a 4-week tail describes doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Once daily with a 1-2 day lead-in and a 7-day tail describes atovaquone-proguanil and primaquine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No listed regimen combines weekly dosing with a 1-2 day lead-in and a 7-day tail.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A 3-week lead-in with a 4-week tail describes mefloquine.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with cirrhosis and chronic kidney disease has documented normal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase activity and is to receive primaquine after an episode of Plasmodium vivax malaria. Which of the following best describes the dosing consideration for this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No dosage adjustment is required for renal or hepatic impairment

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dose must be doubled because hepatic clearance is increased

choices.label: C
choices.text: The dose must be halved in the presence of hepatic impairment

choices.label: D
choices.text: The drug is contraindicated once creatinine clearance falls

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug should be given weekly rather than daily in renal disease

explanation.summary: Primaquine is well tolerated and needs no renal or hepatic dose adjustment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Primaquine is well tolerated by most patients and does not require any dosage adjustments for kidney or liver disease. Its notable risks are cardiac arrhythmias with QT prolongation, leukopenia, and hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency, which has been excluded here.

whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no recommendation to increase the primaquine dose in liver disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No hepatic dose reduction is described for primaquine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Renal elimination and avoidance in severe renal failure apply to atovaquone-proguanil, not primaquine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primaquine is dosed once daily; weekly dosing applies to chloroquine and mefloquine.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman started hydroxychloroquine prophylaxis 2 days ago and calls about generalized itching. She has no rash, fever, dyspnea, or dark urine. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continue the drug, because pruritus is common and often resolves in 48-72 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue the drug, but obtain a G6PD level to confirm ongoing hemolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop the drug, because pruritus is the earliest sign of drug-induced cardiomyopathy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stop the drug, because pruritus signals allergy to chloroquine compounds

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to mefloquine, which does not produce pruritus at any dose

explanation.summary: Pruritus is the most common adverse effect of chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine and is usually self-limited.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine are generally well tolerated. One of the more common adverse effects is pruritus, and it often resolves within 48-72 hours, so the drug can be continued in a patient with no other findings.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemolysis occurs in G6PD deficiency and would present with anemia and dark urine, not isolated pruritus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cardiomyopathy and EKG changes are rare concerns with these drugs and do not present as itching.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Allergy to chloroquine and related compounds is a contraindication, but isolated self-limited pruritus is an expected effect rather than an allergic reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mefloquine carries a black box warning for neuropsychiatric disorders and is not a preferred substitute for transient itching.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: An antimalarial agent used for both prophylaxis and treatment is associated with pruritus, EKG changes with cardiomyopathy, and hemolysis in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. Which of the following is this drug?

explanation.summary: The triad of pruritus, cardiomyopathy with EKG changes, and G6PD hemolysis identifies chloroquine.
explanation.whyCorrect: The malaria drugs summary lists chloroquine's adverse effects as pruritus, EKG changes and cardiomyopathy, and hemolysis in G6PD deficiency, with caution advised in patients with significant cardiac history.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Artemisinins cause hypotension, dizziness, and ataxia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Atovaquone-proguanil causes nausea, abdominal pain, and transaminitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline causes GI disturbances and photosensitivity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mefloquine causes abnormal dreams and insomnia and carries a neuropsychiatric black box warning.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man taking atovaquone-proguanil for prophylaxis is found on routine testing to have an AST of 96 U/L and an ALT of 88 U/L. He is asymptomatic, and renal function is normal. Which of the following is the most likely course of these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Further rise accompanied by hemolysis and indirect hyperbilirubinemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Persistent elevation that requires indefinite hepatology follow-up

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progression to fulminant hepatic failure within several days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resolution only after the patient undergoes plasma exchange

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transient elevation that resolves within about 4 weeks

explanation.summary: Transaminitis from atovaquone-proguanil is generally transient and self-resolving.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some of the most common adverse reactions to atovaquone-proguanil are abdominal pain, nausea, and increases in the liver enzymes AST and ALT. The transaminitis is generally transient and self-resolving within 4 weeks or less.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemolysis with indirect hyperbilirubinemia relates to primaquine or chloroquine in G6PD deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The enzyme elevation is self-limited rather than persistent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fulminant hepatic failure is not a described consequence of this drug's transaminitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No exchange or extracorporeal therapy is required for a transient transaminitis.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: Proguanil is combined with atovaquone because the two agents act synergistically. The active metabolite of proguanil kills Plasmodium by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cleaving an endoperoxide bridge to generate free radicals

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase and parasite folate synthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibiting mitochondrial electron transport in the parasite

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibiting the parasite ribosome at the 30S subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Preventing conversion of heme to hemozoin in the vacuole

explanation.summary: Proguanil's active metabolite inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, blocking folate-dependent DNA synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Atovaquone selectively inhibits mitochondrial electron transport of the parasite, while proguanil's active metabolite interferes with parasite folate synthesis used in DNA synthesis by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase. The two components therefore act at different steps.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cleavage of an endoperoxide bridge by Fe2+ with free-radical formation describes the artemisinins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mitochondrial electron transport inhibition is the atovaquone component, not proguanil.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The 30S ribosomal subunit is the target of doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Interference with heme-to-hemozoin conversion is the action of chloroquine.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A traveler is counseled that his prophylactic agent acts at both the erythrocytic and exoerythrocytic stages of development and therefore treats active liver schizonts as well as blood-stage parasites. Which of the following agents was prescribed?

explanation.summary: Atovaquone and proguanil together affect erythrocytic and exoerythrocytic stages, including active liver schizonts.
explanation.whyCorrect: Together, atovaquone and proguanil affect the erythrocytic and exoerythrocytic stages of development, meaning the medication is effective in treating active liver schizonts as well as the blood-stage parasite. This dual-stage coverage underlies its short 7-day post-travel course.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Artemether-lumefantrine is a treatment combination acting on blood-stage parasites through free-radical damage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chloroquine acts on heme metabolism within the digestive vacuole of blood-stage parasites.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doxycycline inhibits protein synthesis at the 30S subunit and is not described as treating liver schizonts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mefloquine is thought to interfere with protein synthesis and hemoglobin digestion in the blood stage.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: Mefloquine is chemically similar to quinine and is widely available in the United States. Which of the following is thought to be its principal antimalarial mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increasing digestive vacuole pH to block hemozoin formation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase within the parasite

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of protein synthesis at the 30S subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Interference with protein synthesis at the 80S subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Selective inhibition of mitochondrial electron transport

explanation.summary: Mefloquine is classified as a protein synthesis inhibitor acting at the 80S subunit.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mefloquine's specific mechanism is not fully understood, but it is thought to interfere with protein synthesis of Plasmodium spp. at the 80S subunit, and it may also interfere with hemoglobin digestion. It is listed in the drug summary as a protein synthesis inhibitor (80S).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Raising vacuole pH so that toxic heme accumulates is the action of chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dihydrofolate reductase inhibition is the action of proguanil.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The 30S subunit is the target of doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mitochondrial electron transport inhibition is the action of atovaquone.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman who had a severe allergic reaction to quinidine several years ago now requires malaria chemoprophylaxis. Which of the following drugs should be avoided?

explanation.summary: Mefloquine is contraindicated in patients allergic to quinine or quinidine because of structural similarity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mefloquine's chemical structure is similar to quinine, and its listed contraindications include allergy to similar compounds, specifically mefloquine, quinine, and quinidine, in addition to a history of seizures or psychiatric issues.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Artemisinins are contraindicated only in patients with allergy to artemisinins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Atovaquone-proguanil is contraindicated in severe renal failure and is unrelated to quinidine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is contraindicated with allergy to tetracyclines and with coadministered cations, not with quinidine allergy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primaquine is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency and in patients at risk for granulocytopenia.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man receiving cytotoxic chemotherapy has a neutrophil count of 900/mm3 and is considered at risk for granulocytopenia. His glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase activity is normal. Which of the following antimalarial drugs is contraindicated?

explanation.summary: Primaquine causes leukopenia and is contraindicated in patients at risk for granulocytopenia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The malaria drugs summary lists primaquine's adverse effects as cardiac arrhythmia and leukopenia, and its contraindications as G6PD deficiency with hemolytic anemia and patients at risk for granulocytopenia. A neutropenic chemotherapy patient falls into the latter group even with normal G6PD activity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atovaquone's associated contraindication is severe renal failure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chloroquine is contraindicated with allergy to chloroquine and related compounds; its hematologic risk is hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is contraindicated with tetracycline allergy or coadministered cations, not with granulocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mefloquine is contraindicated with quinine-class allergy, seizures, or psychiatric disease.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man returning from West Africa has symptomatic Plasmodium falciparum malaria with 3% of erythrocytes parasitized. Which of the following additional findings would classify his infection as complicated malaria?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arterial pH of 7.24 with bicarbonate of 12 mEq/L

choices.label: D
choices.text: Palpable splenic tip on abdominal examination

choices.label: E
choices.text: Temperature of 39.2 C with shaking chills

explanation.summary: Metabolic acidosis is one of the defining features of complicated malaria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complicated malaria is characterized by hypoglycemia, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, metabolic acidosis, and jaundice, together with major signs of organ dysfunction such as pulmonary edema or convulsions, or more than 4% of RBCs infected. An arterial pH of 7.24 with a low bicarbonate is metabolic acidosis and therefore defines complicated disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Myalgias and headache are nonspecific symptoms and are not among the defining criteria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A hemoglobin of 12.8 g/dL is normal and argues against the severe anemia seen in complicated malaria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Splenomegaly is not listed among the features that define complicated malaria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fever with chills is the symptomatic presentation of malaria in general and does not by itself define complicated disease.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: In classifying the severity of a symptomatic Plasmodium falciparum infection, malaria is considered complicated when the proportion of infected erythrocytes exceeds which of the following?

explanation.summary: A parasitemia greater than 4% of infected RBCs marks complicated malaria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uncomplicated malaria is defined as symptomatic infection with parasitemia below 4% of RBCs infected and no sign of organ dysfunction, whereas complicated malaria includes more than 4% of RBCs infected along with features such as hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and jaundice.

whyWrongByChoice.A: One percent is below the threshold and falls within the uncomplicated range.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Two percent is still below the stated threshold for complicated disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ten percent exceeds the threshold but is not the cut point used for the classification.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Twenty percent is far above the defined cut point and is not the stated criterion.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: Artemisinins for uncomplicated malaria are most often supplied as a single combination tablet containing a partner drug. Which of the following is a quinine derivative used as that partner agent?

explanation.summary: Artemisinins are partnered with the quinine derivatives lumefantrine, amodiaquine, or mefloquine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Artemisinin medications are most often available in a single combination tablet, and they are most often combined with the quinine derivatives lumefantrine, amodiaquine, or mefloquine. Artemether-lumefantrine is the leading example of such an ACT regimen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atovaquone is partnered with proguanil for malaria and with azithromycin for babesiosis, not with artemisinins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Azithromycin is a macrolide used in the first-line babesiosis regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gentamicin is the aminoglycoside used with doxycycline for brucellosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primaquine is used to prevent relapse from exoerythrocytic stages and is not an ACT partner drug.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with uncomplicated falciparum malaria acquired in a chloroquine-resistant region is prescribed oral artemether-lumefantrine. Which of the following is the correct regimen?

explanation.summary: Oral artemether-lumefantrine is given twice daily for 3 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ACT therapies listed give artemether-lumefantrine orally twice daily for 3 days, whereas artesunate-amodiaquine and artesunate-mefloquine are given orally once daily for 3 days and intravenous artesunate is given for 24 hours before switching to oral therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No ACT regimen is completed with a single oral dose.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Once daily for 7 days does not match any listed ACT regimen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Weekly dosing applies to chloroquine and mefloquine prophylaxis, not to ACT treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 14-day course is longer than any listed ACT regimen.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man being treated with an artemisinin combination tablet for uncomplicated malaria reports lightheadedness and an unsteady, staggering gait. His blood pressure is 92/58 mm Hg. These findings are best explained by which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Artemisinin-triggered hemolysis in underlying G6PD deficiency

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expected adverse effects of artemisinin-based therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nephrotoxicity produced by an aminoglycoside component

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neuropsychiatric toxicity that carries a black box warning

choices.label: E
choices.text: Photosensitivity reaction typical of the tetracycline class

explanation.summary: Hypotension, dizziness, and ataxia are the generalized adverse effects of ACT.
explanation.whyCorrect: ACT has a low adverse effect profile, which is part of why it is preferred first-line therapy, but the generalized adverse effects of hypotension, dizziness, and ataxia are the main ones to watch for. This patient's unsteady gait, lightheadedness, and low blood pressure fit that pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemolysis in G6PD deficiency is associated with primaquine and chloroquine, not with artemisinins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity applies to gentamicin used for brucellosis; no aminoglycoside is present in ACT.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The neuropsychiatric black box warning belongs to mefloquine when used as a single prophylactic agent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Photosensitivity is an adverse effect of doxycycline.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman has falciparum malaria with 9% parasitemia, jaundice, and confusion. The pharmacy reports that intravenous artesunate will not be available for several hours. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Start intravenous doxycycline until intravenous artesunate arrives

choices.label: B
choices.text: Start oral artemether-lumefantrine until intravenous artesunate arrives

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start oral chloroquine until intravenous artesunate arrives

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start oral primaquine until intravenous artesunate arrives

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold antimalarial therapy until intravenous artesunate arrives

explanation.summary: When IV artesunate is delayed in severe malaria, a fast-acting oral agent is started immediately.
explanation.whyCorrect: If intravenous artesunate is not readily available, fast-acting oral medications such as artemether-lumefantrine, atovaquone-proguanil, or mefloquine should be initiated immediately and continued until intravenous artesunate is available.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Intravenous or oral doxycycline should be avoided in severe malaria because it is slow-acting relative to other agents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Chloroquine is not among the fast-acting bridging options and is ineffective where resistance is present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primaquine targets dormant exoerythrocytic forms of P. ovale and P. vivax and is not a fast-acting bridge for severe falciparum disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Delaying therapy is inappropriate in complicated malaria, where treatment must begin immediately.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with babesiosis is started on azithromycin plus atovaquone. He takes several other medications metabolized by CYP3A4. Besides drug interactions, which of the following adverse effects of azithromycin should be monitored?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Photosensitivity and chelation by dietary cations

explanation.summary: Azithromycin is generally well tolerated but can cause QT prolongation and GI upset and interacts through CYP3A4.
explanation.whyCorrect: Azithromycin is a macrolide protein synthesis inhibitor that is generally well tolerated, but common adverse effects include QT prolongation and GI upset, and watching for CYP3A4 drug interactions is warranted.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abnormal dreams and insomnia are characteristic of mefloquine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemolysis in G6PD deficiency is a risk with primaquine and chloroquine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity are the key aminoglycoside toxicities seen with gentamicin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Photosensitivity and cation chelation are characteristic of doxycycline.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A patient with babesiosis cannot tolerate the first-line regimen and is switched to clindamycin plus mefloquine. Clindamycin inhibits protein synthesis at which of the following sites?

explanation.summary: Clindamycin, like azithromycin, is a 50S protein synthesis inhibitor.
explanation.whyCorrect: The alternative babesiosis regimen, used if the first-line combination is not available or not tolerated, is clindamycin plus mefloquine. Clindamycin is a protein synthesis inhibitor at the 50S subunit, and its adverse effects and interactions are similar to those of azithromycin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The 30S subunit is the target of doxycycline and the aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The 40S subunit is not identified as the target of any drug in this material.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The 60S subunit is not identified as the target of any drug in this material.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The 80S subunit is the proposed target of mefloquine, the partner drug in this regimen.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old dairy worker with brucellosis is started on doxycycline plus gentamicin. These two drugs share which of the following properties?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both act on the 50S ribosomal subunit of the organism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both are chelated by dietary cations found in multivitamins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both are contraindicated in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both inhibit protein synthesis at the 30S ribosomal subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Both require dose reduction in the presence of hepatic impairment

explanation.summary: Doxycycline and gentamicin, the first-line brucellosis pair, are both 30S protein synthesis inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: The drugs used for brucellosis are doxycycline and an aminoglycoside, usually gentamicin, and both of these medications are protein synthesis inhibitors at the 30S subunit. Their adverse effect profiles differ, with chelation and photosensitivity for doxycycline and nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity for gentamicin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The 50S subunit is the target of azithromycin and clindamycin, which are used for babesiosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chelation by cations such as magnesium and iron is specific to tetracyclines like doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neither agent is listed as contraindicated in G6PD deficiency; that applies to primaquine and chloroquine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No hepatic dose adjustment is described for either agent in this regimen.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman being treated for uncomplicated malaria asks how quickly the medication works. With appropriate treatment, the parasite is usually cleared from the body within which of the following time frames?

explanation.summary: The prognosis for malaria is good, with parasite clearance usually within 48 hours of appropriate treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: The prognosis for malaria is good with appropriate treatment, and the parasite is usually cleared from the body within 48 hours. Artemisinin combination therapy in particular produces the most rapid clearance of Plasmodium spp. relative to the other antimalarial drugs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Three weeks corresponds to the preferable mefloquine lead-in before exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Six hours is shorter than the stated clearance interval.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Six weeks far exceeds the stated time to parasite clearance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Seven days corresponds to the post-travel prophylactic course for atovaquone-proguanil, not to parasite clearance.

questions.topicName: Drugs to Treat Plasmodium spp., Babesia spp., and Brucella spp.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with fever, fatigue, nausea, and diarrhea 5 days after returning from a 2-week safari in Uganda. Her hospital course is complicated by pancytopenia, markedly elevated AST and ALT, coagulopathy, and mucosal bleeding. Serologic testing eventually reveals IgG specific for Marburg virus. To which of the following viral families does the causative agent belong?

explanation.summary: Marburg and Ebola viruses are the two genera of the family Filoviridae.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Filoviridae family includes the genera Marburgvirus and Ebolavirus. Filoviruses are filamentous, enveloped viruses with a helical capsid and a linear, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genome, and they cause the most rapidly progressive of the viral hemorrhagic fevers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Arenaviridae includes Lassa fever virus, a rodent-associated cause of VHF, not Marburg virus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bunyaviridae includes hantavirus and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus, not the filoviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Flaviviridae includes the mosquito-borne arboviruses such as yellow fever, dengue, West Nile, and Zika.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Togaviruses (e.g., chikungunya, EEV/WEV) are mosquito-borne arboviruses unrelated to Marburg virus.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 29-year-old geologist develops fever, chills, and myalgias followed by vomiting and mucosal bleeding about 10 days after exploring bat-inhabited caves in central Africa. Laboratory studies show thrombocytopenia, elevated transaminases, and prolonged coagulation times, and Marburg virus disease is confirmed. Which of the following is the natural reservoir of the responsible virus?

explanation.summary: Bats are the reservoir for Marburg virus and the likely reservoir for Ebola virus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bats are the confirmed reservoir for Marburg virus and the likely reservoir for Ebola virus. Human spillover can occur with exposure in caves or mines inhabited by bats, after which filoviruses spread between people through contact with infected bodily fluids.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mosquitoes transmit arboviral hemorrhagic fevers such as yellow fever and dengue, not Marburg virus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rodents such as deer mice are the reservoir for hantavirus, not for the filoviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Swine are not a recognized reservoir for Marburg or Ebola virus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ticks transmit Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, not filovirus disease.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man from rural New Mexico presents with several days of fever, myalgias, and nausea that abruptly progress to severe hypotension, dyspnea, and hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring intubation. He recently cleaned a rodent-infested shed. Chest imaging shows bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome is diagnosed. Which of the following best explains his pulmonary findings?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pulmonary embolism with focal perfusion defects

choices.label: D
choices.text: Secondary bacterial pneumonia of the lower lobes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upper airway obstruction from laryngeal edema

explanation.summary: HCPS causes noncardiogenic pulmonary edema from capillary leak into the pulmonary bed.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome features a nonspecific prodrome followed by rapid onset of hypotension and pulmonary edema caused by capillary leak into the pulmonary bed. The increased vascular permeability floods the alveoli, producing bilateral infiltrates and respiratory failure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The edema is noncardiogenic; it results from vascular leak rather than pump failure of the left ventricle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pulmonary embolism causes focal perfusion defects, not the diffuse capillary-leak edema seen in HCPS.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Features of respiratory tract infection such as rhinorrhea and pharyngitis are absent in HCPS, and the edema is from capillary leak, not a bacterial process.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The disease affects the pulmonary vasculature and alveoli, not the upper airway.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man develops fever, myalgias, and progressive dyspnea. He lives in a rural area and had recently swept out a barn heavily contaminated with mouse droppings and urine. Hantavirus infection is suspected. Which of the following is the most likely route by which he acquired the virus?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct contact with an infected person's bodily fluids

explanation.summary: Hantavirus is acquired mainly by inhaling aerosolized rodent excreta.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hantavirus transmission is due to rodent contact, including feces, urine, and saliva. Inhalation of aerosolized particles or ingestion of virions are the known routes of infection, and disturbing contaminated droppings generates infectious aerosols.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mosquito transmission applies to arboviruses such as yellow fever and dengue, not hantavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tick-borne transmission applies to Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, not hantavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Person-to-person spread through bodily fluids characterizes the filoviruses Ebola and Marburg, not hantavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Filovirus spillover can involve infected animals, but hantavirus is chiefly acquired by inhaling rodent excreta.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 24-year-old soldier stationed in South Korea develops fever, headache, and back pain, followed by petechiae, hypotension, and a rising serum creatinine with oliguria. He recalls exposure to field rodents. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his illness?

explanation.summary: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome is caused by Old World hantaviruses in Asia and Europe.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is characterized by fever, hemorrhage, hypotension, and acute kidney injury. More than 95% of hantavirus cases are due to Old World hantaviruses, which occur in Asia and Europe, matching this soldier's rodent exposure in Korea.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ebola virus causes hepatic injury and diffuse hemorrhage in Central and West Africa, not a rodent-linked renal syndrome in Asia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lassa fever occurs in West Africa; the geography and renal-predominant syndrome here point to Old World hantavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Marburg virus is a bat-associated filovirus of Central Africa, not the cause of rodent-linked HFRS.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne flaviviral illness, not a rodent-associated renal syndrome.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A public health team is comparing the clinical features of Ebola virus disease, Marburg virus disease, and hantavirus infection. Which of the following findings would be expected in hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome but not in filovirus disease?

choices.label: C
choices.text: High case-fatality rate of 50% or more

explanation.summary: Respiratory failure from noncardiogenic pulmonary edema is a hallmark of HCPS, not filovirus disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Respiratory failure due to pulmonary edema from capillary leak is a hallmark of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome and is not a feature of Ebola or Marburg virus disease, whose severe manifestations center on hepatic injury, DIC, and diffuse hemorrhage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DIC occurs in severe filovirus disease and in severe HFRS, so it is not unique to hantavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Elevated liver enzymes are especially prominent in filovirus infection, which causes hepatocellular injury.
