whyWrongByChoice.C: Filoviruses carry a high case-fatality rate (about 50-60%), so this does not separate hantavirus from them.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thrombocytopenia is common to all of these viral hemorrhagic fevers and does not distinguish hantavirus.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 31-year-old healthcare worker who cared for patients during an Ebola outbreak develops fever and myalgias with any possible risk of exposure. Which of the following is the standard laboratory method to confirm Ebola virus disease?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gram stain of a buffy coat smear

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thick and thin peripheral blood smears

explanation.summary: RT-PCR for viral RNA in blood is the standard of laboratory testing for filovirus disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Real-time reverse transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR) for viral RNA in blood is the standard of laboratory testing for filovirus disease and should be performed in symptomatic patients with any possible exposure. Rapid immunoassays for Ebola antigens can provide a provisional diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blood cultures detect bacteria and fungi, not the viral RNA needed to diagnose Ebola.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gram stain identifies bacteria and is not used to diagnose a viral hemorrhagic fever.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stool ova and parasite testing evaluates parasitic infections, not Ebola virus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Blood smears are used to diagnose malaria and babesiosis, not filovirus infection.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman recovering from a suspected hantavirus infection is being evaluated to confirm the diagnosis. Which of the following laboratory tests is most appropriate to confirm hantavirus infection?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Peripheral blood smear for intracellular parasites

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serology for virus-specific IgM and IgG antibodies

explanation.summary: Hantavirus infection is confirmed with serologic testing; symptomatic patients typically have both IgM and IgG.
explanation.whyCorrect: The diagnosis of hantavirus infection is confirmed with serologic tests, and symptomatic patients typically have both IgM and IgG to hantavirus. Diagnosis is otherwise supported by a history of rodent exposure and compatible clinical and laboratory findings.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bone marrow biopsy is not part of the workup for hantavirus infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A blood smear for intracellular parasites is used for malaria or babesiosis, not hantavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sputum culture identifies bacterial pathogens, not a viral hemorrhagic fever.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Legionella urine antigen testing evaluates a bacterial pneumonia, not hantavirus.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A patient with confirmed Ebola virus disease is treated with one of the FDA-approved monoclonal antibody therapies in addition to aggressive supportive care. Which of the following best describes the primary mechanism by which these antibodies neutralize the virus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocking binding of a viral surface glycoprotein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibiting a viral protease required for maturation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibiting the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Preventing viral genome uncoating in the endosome

explanation.summary: The approved anti-Ebola monoclonal antibodies block the viral glycoprotein from binding host receptors.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two monoclonal antibody therapies are FDA-approved for the treatment of Ebola virus disease, and all block the binding of a viral surface glycoprotein to cognate host receptors, thereby neutralizing the virus. They additionally mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity in vitro.

whyWrongByChoice.B: These therapies neutralize by blocking receptor binding, not by inhibiting a viral protease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The approved antibodies act on the surface glycoprotein rather than inhibiting the viral polymerase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Filoviruses do not have neuraminidase; neuraminidase inhibitors are used against influenza.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The antibodies prevent viral attachment and entry rather than acting on genome uncoating.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: During an outbreak response, a public health official is deciding which exposed contacts and frontline healthcare workers can be offered vaccination. For which of the following viruses is a vaccine currently available to protect immediate contacts and high-risk workers?

explanation.summary: Viral vector vaccines are available for Ebola virus but not for Marburg or hantavirus.
explanation.whyCorrect: For Ebola virus disease, viral vector vaccines are stockpiled and available for outbreak responses, including vaccination of immediate contacts, frontline healthcare workers in high-risk countries, and those who research the virus. No approved vaccine exists for Marburg virus disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: No vaccine is available for the New World hantaviruses that cause HCPS.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There is no approved vaccine for hantavirus; prevention relies on avoiding rodent excreta.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick describes an available vaccine for Ebola, not for Lassa fever virus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There are no approved vaccines for Marburg virus disease.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with confirmed Ebola virus disease is 8 days into his illness and appears critically ill. Which of the following laboratory patterns is most consistent with severe filovirus disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Isolated neutropenia with normal coagulation studies

choices.label: B
choices.text: Normal platelet count with low transaminases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thrombocytopenia with prolonged PT and PTT

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thrombocytosis with a shortened prothrombin time

explanation.summary: Severe VHF shows thrombocytopenia, prolonged clotting times, and elevated transaminases reflecting DIC and hepatic injury.
explanation.whyCorrect: For all VHFs, thrombocytopenia is common and transaminases (AST, ALT) may be elevated, reflecting liver involvement. Consistent with DIC, the prothrombin time (PT) and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) are prolonged and fibrin degradation products are elevated in severe disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coagulation studies are abnormal in severe disease because of DIC, and platelets fall rather than remaining normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Platelets fall and transaminases rise because of hepatic injury, opposite to the pattern described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DIC consumes clotting factors and platelets; polycythemia and elevated fibrinogen are not expected.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Severe filovirus disease causes thrombocytopenia and prolonged, not shortened, coagulation times.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 40-year-old aid worker is evaluated after possible exposure to a filovirus. She is counseled that symptoms may not appear immediately and that she should monitor for illness. According to the typical incubation period of filovirus disease, symptoms may begin as long as which of the following after exposure?

explanation.summary: Filovirus symptoms may begin as little as 2 or as many as 21 days after exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the dry phase of filovirus disease, symptoms may begin as little as 2 or as many as 21 days after exposure, starting with the abrupt onset of nonspecific flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills, myalgia, and fatigue. This roughly 3-week outer limit guides post-exposure monitoring.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A one-year incubation is far longer than the described 2- to 21-day window for filoviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Onset can occur around 2-3 days but may be delayed up to 21 days, so 3 days is not the maximum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The incubation period is measured in days to a few weeks, not months.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The minimum incubation is about 2 days, so 24 hours understates the typical onset window.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A virology laboratory characterizes an enveloped virus with a helical capsid isolated from a 40-year-old woman in rural Finland who developed fever, hypotension, and acute kidney injury after field mice infested her home. Which of the following best describes the genome of the causative agent?

explanation.summary: Hantavirus is a bunyavirus, and bunyavirus genomes are circular, segmented, negative-sense single-stranded RNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hantavirus is a bunyavirus with an envelope surrounding a helical capsid. Bunyavirus genomes are circular, segmented, and made of negative-sense, single-stranded RNA, which distinguishes them from the filoviruses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemorrhagic viruses are RNA viruses; none of them carry a DNA genome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bunyavirus RNA is negative-sense rather than positive-sense.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A linear, nonsegmented negative-sense RNA genome describes the filoviruses Ebola and Marburg, not hantavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The hemorrhagic viruses discussed here are single-stranded RNA viruses, not double-stranded RNA viruses.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man in Sierra Leone with RT-PCR-confirmed Ebola virus disease has had 3 days of fever, chills, myalgia, and fatigue without other complaints. His family asks what is likely to happen next. Approximately 4 to 5 days after symptom onset, which of the following groups of findings is most likely to appear?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Jaundice with pale stools and severe pruritus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Migratory polyarthritis and a malar rash

choices.label: D
choices.text: Productive cough with purulent sputum and pleuritic chest pain

explanation.summary: Filovirus disease progresses from a dry phase of flu-like symptoms to a wet phase of gastrointestinal symptoms 4 to 5 days after onset.
explanation.whyCorrect: Filovirus disease can be divided into a dry phase and a wet phase. Four to five days after symptom onset, patients progress from nonspecific flu-like illness to gastrointestinal symptoms: diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Although hepatic injury is profound, obstructive features such as pale stools and pruritus are not the expected progression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Polyarthritis and a malar rash are features of connective tissue disease, not the wet phase of filovirus disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Purulent sputum and pleuritic pain suggest bacterial pneumonia; the wet phase is defined by gastrointestinal symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Upper respiratory features are not part of the described filovirus course; chest pain and shortness of breath may occur instead.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man is hospitalized with confirmed Marburg virus disease and has entered the wet phase with vomiting and diarrhea. His wife asks how likely he is to develop bleeding such as petechiae, ecchymosis, or mucosal hemorrhage. Approximately what proportion of patients with filovirus disease develop bleeding manifestations?

explanation.summary: Bleeding is present in roughly 40% of patients with filovirus disease, not in all of them.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bleeding is present in roughly 40% of patients during the wet phase and may manifest as petechiae, ecchymosis, mucosal hemorrhage, or blood in stool or vomit. Despite the name viral hemorrhagic fever, most patients do not bleed overtly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bleeding is far more frequent than this; it occurs in a substantial minority of patients.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This underestimates the frequency of bleeding manifestations in filovirus disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Most patients do not bleed, so a majority figure overstates the frequency.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Universal bleeding is not seen; overt hemorrhage occurs in less than half of patients.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman with Ebola virus disease is deteriorating rapidly with shock, diffuse hemorrhage, and multiorgan failure. Among patients with fatal filovirus disease, death generally occurs at approximately which point after symptom onset?

explanation.summary: Death in fatal filovirus disease generally occurs 8 to 9 days after symptom onset.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fatality averages 50-60% and patients with fatal disease usually display more rapid progression. Death generally occurs 8 to 9 days after symptom onset from disseminated intravascular coagulation, diffuse hemorrhage, multiorgan failure, and septic shock.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The wet phase itself does not begin until 4 to 5 days after onset, so death this early is not typical.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A months-long course is inconsistent with the rapid progression that characterizes filovirus disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Death occurs within the second week of symptoms rather than after a month.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Filovirus disease progresses over days, not within the first day of symptoms.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman is on day 6 of Ebola virus disease with vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. In addition to gastrointestinal symptoms, which of the following findings is commonly seen during this phase of illness?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Splinter hemorrhages of the nail beds

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vesicular rash on the palms and soles

explanation.summary: Eye irritation and redness are common during the wet phase of filovirus disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: During the wet phase, patients may develop chest pain, shortness of breath, headache, confusion, or seizures in addition to gastrointestinal symptoms. Eye irritation and redness are common findings in this phase.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hearing loss is not among the described manifestations of the wet phase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Painless genital ulceration suggests primary syphilis and is unrelated to filovirus disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Splinter hemorrhages suggest endocarditis rather than filovirus infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A vesicular acral rash is not a feature of filovirus disease as described.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man with a viral hemorrhagic fever has laboratory studies showing elevated amylase, elevated aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase, prolonged prothrombin and partial thromboplastin times, elevated fibrin degradation products, and thrombocytopenia. Which of the following abnormalities specifically reflects pancreatic involvement?

explanation.summary: In viral hemorrhagic fever, an elevated amylase reflects pancreatic involvement while the transaminases reflect liver involvement.
explanation.whyCorrect: For all VHFs, amylase, AST, and ALT may be elevated, reflecting pancreatic and liver involvement respectively. Amylase is the marker attributable to the pancreas in this panel.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Elevated ALT reflects hepatocellular injury, which is prominent in filovirus disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Elevated fibrin degradation products indicate ongoing DIC rather than pancreatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A prolonged PTT reflects the consumptive coagulopathy of DIC, not pancreatic injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thrombocytopenia is common to all VHFs and reflects platelet consumption, not pancreatic involvement.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman admitted with a viral hemorrhagic fever has a white blood cell count of 2,100/microliter on hospital day 2. By hospital day 7 her white blood cell count has risen to 14,300/microliter with numerous band forms. Which of the following best describes the expected evolution of the white blood cell count in viral hemorrhagic fever?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Early neutrophilia followed by profound lymphocytosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Initial leukopenia followed by neutrophilia with a left shift

choices.label: C
choices.text: Marked eosinophilia beginning at symptom onset

choices.label: D
choices.text: Normal leukocyte count with isolated monocytosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sustained leukopenia that persists through recovery

explanation.summary: VHF laboratory findings include initial leukopenia followed later by elevated neutrophils and a left shift.
explanation.whyCorrect: For all VHFs, laboratory findings may include initial leukopenia followed later by elevated neutrophils and a left shift. The rising count with band forms on day 7 is the expected later pattern rather than a superimposed process.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The sequence is reversed: leukopenia comes first and neutrophils rise later.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Eosinophilia is not a described feature of viral hemorrhagic fever.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The white cell count is not expected to remain normal; it falls and then rises.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Leukopenia is an early finding that is followed by a rise in neutrophils.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man in Ohio presents with fever, myalgia, and vomiting. He has no history of international travel, no contact with animals, and no known contact with an ill person. RT-PCR is positive for Ebola virus. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin empiric antimalarial therapy and observe

choices.label: B
choices.text: Promptly report the case to local and state health authorities

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reassure the patient and arrange outpatient follow-up

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat the travel history in 2 weeks before acting

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer care to an outpatient infectious disease clinic

explanation.summary: Ebola virus is a CDC Category A bioterror agent, and a case without exposure history should be reported promptly.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ebola virus is classified as a Category A bioterror agent by the CDC. In a bioterror attack, patients would present with no history of travel to Central or West Africa and no other possible exposure to an infected animal or Ebola patient, and any clinician suspecting bioterrorism should report it promptly to local and state health authorities.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Malaria is a mimic to exclude, but RT-PCR has already confirmed Ebola virus in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Confirmed filovirus disease requires containment and aggressive supportive care, not outpatient reassurance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Delaying action for 2 weeks forgoes both infection control and prompt notification.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An outpatient clinic cannot provide the containment and supportive care this patient requires.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man returns from Liberia and develops abrupt fever, chills, and myalgia. Filovirus disease is considered, and the evaluation includes testing for other febrile diseases with a similar presentation and geographic distribution. Which of the following is the most likely alternative diagnosis in this patient?

explanation.summary: Malaria is one of the febrile illnesses most commonly confused with the much rarer filovirus disease in returning travelers from West Africa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Typhoid fever, meningococcemia, pneumonia, and malaria can all be confused with the much rarer filovirus disease. Assessment should include evaluation for other febrile diseases with similar presentation and geographic distribution, and malaria fits both the syndrome and travel to Liberia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Coccidioidomycosis is acquired in the southwestern United States, not West Africa.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HCPS is caused by New World hantaviruses isolated to the Americas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lyme disease occurs in temperate North America and Europe and does not match this travel history.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is a tick-borne illness of the Americas and does not fit this geography.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: During an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, a field clinic without molecular testing capability evaluates a febrile patient using a rapid immunoassay for Ebola virus antigens, which returns positive. Which of the following best describes how this result should be interpreted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It definitively confirms disease, so no further testing is needed

choices.label: B
choices.text: It detects antibodies and indicates remote past infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: It excludes infection whenever a single specimen is negative

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the preferred confirmatory test for Marburg virus disease

choices.label: E
choices.text: It provides a provisional diagnosis pending RT-PCR confirmation

explanation.summary: Rapid antigen immunoassays give a provisional diagnosis of EVD; RT-PCR remains the standard of laboratory testing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rapid immunoassays for Ebola virus antigens can provide a provisional diagnosis of EVD, but real-time reverse transcriptase PCR for viral RNA in blood is the standard of laboratory testing for filovirus disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The rapid assay is provisional; confirmation still rests on RT-PCR.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These assays detect viral antigen rather than antibody, so they indicate current infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A provisional test cannot be used to rule out infection in a symptomatic exposed patient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rapid tests for Marburg virus were not yet field-tested as of October 2025.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A global health fellow reviews the World Health Organization estimate that roughly 30,000 cases of Ebola virus disease and fewer than 1,000 cases of Marburg virus disease have occurred to date. Which of the following best characterizes Marburg virus disease relative to Ebola virus disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is less contagious and produces smaller outbreaks

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is more contagious and produces larger outbreaks

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is spread mainly by rodents rather than by bats

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is transmitted by mosquitoes rather than bodily fluids

choices.label: E
choices.text: It occurs more often in the Americas than in Africa

explanation.summary: Marburg virus is less contagious than Ebola virus, and its outbreaks tend to be smaller.
explanation.whyCorrect: Filovirus infections are rare, with roughly 30,000 EVD and fewer than 1,000 MVD cases to date. Marburg virus is less contagious, and outbreaks tend to be smaller.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The far smaller case total reflects lower contagiousness and smaller outbreaks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bats are the reservoir for Marburg virus; rodents are reservoirs for hantaviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both filoviruses are transmitted through contact with infected bodily fluids, not by mosquitoes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vast majority of MVD and EVD cases have occurred in Central and West Africa.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: An outbreak investigation reviews a cluster of filovirus infections among hospital staff, who in some outbreaks have accounted for as much as 100% of Ebola virus disease cases and 50% of Marburg virus disease cases. Which of the following exposure situations is most commonly implicated in these healthcare-associated infections?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Airborne spread from ventilated patients and contaminated ventilation systems

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumption of contaminated food and shared water in hospital cafeterias

choices.label: C
choices.text: Handling of hospital laundry and mosquito bites on hospital grounds

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inadequate protective equipment and care of patients with unrecognized infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Needlestick injuries during vaccination and laboratory centrifuge accidents

explanation.summary: Inadequate personal protective equipment and exposure to patients with unrecognized infection are the most common risk situations for healthcare-associated filovirus infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Depending on the outbreak, healthcare workers account for 2%-100% of EVD and 5%-50% of MVD cases. The most common exposure risk situations were inadequate personal protective equipment and exposure to patients with unrecognized infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Filoviruses spread through contact with infected bodily fluids rather than through ventilation systems.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Foodborne and waterborne spread within hospitals is not a described route for filoviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Filoviruses are not arthropod-borne, and laundry handling is not the leading implicated exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sharps and laboratory mishaps are not the leading described exposure situations in these outbreaks.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: In Guinea, a woman dies of Ebola virus disease and several family members wash and prepare her body for burial. Within 2 weeks, three of them develop fever, myalgia, and vomiting and test positive for Ebola virus. Which of the following best explains this transmission event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Body fluids from a deceased person remain infectious

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contaminated drinking water at the funeral spread the virus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Latent virus in the family members reactivated after stress

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mosquitoes at the burial site transmitted the virus

choices.label: E
choices.text: The virus became airborne after the death of the host

explanation.summary: Filovirus-containing body fluids remain infectious even when they originate from a deceased person.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once spillover has occurred, filoviruses spread between people through infected body fluids, and fluids can be infectious even when originating from a deceased person. Prevention requires avoiding contact with bodily fluids of infected or deceased people and animals.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Waterborne spread is not a described route of filovirus transmission.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Filovirus disease results from new infection rather than reactivation of latent virus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Filoviruses are not arthropod-borne; they are among the viral hemorrhagic fevers that are not arboviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transmission occurs through direct or indirect contact with infected fluids, including via fomites.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: An epidemiologist describes how outbreaks of Ebola virus disease begin sporadically when the virus enters the human population from its animal reservoir, after which it spreads between non-human primates and people through infected body fluids. The initial entry of the virus into the human population is best termed which of the following?

explanation.summary: Spillover is the sporadic entry of a filovirus from its animal reservoir into the human population.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both MVD and EVD display spillover, meaning the disease enters into the human population sporadically from the animal reservoir. Once spillover has occurred, filoviruses can spread between non-human primates and people through infected body fluids.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antigenic drift describes gradual mutation of viral surface proteins, not reservoir-to-human introduction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Herd immunity describes population-level protection, not an introduction event.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Filoviruses are not arboviruses and are not transmitted by arthropod vectors.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vertical transmission refers to passage from mother to offspring.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A health ministry is comparing the two clinical forms of hantavirus infection and notes that one form is far more common while the other is considerably more lethal. Which of the following best represents the case-fatality rates of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, respectively?

explanation.summary: HFRS carries a case-fatality rate of 1-10%, while HCPS carries a case-fatality rate of 25-50%.
explanation.whyCorrect: While HFRS is more common, it is less deadly than HCPS. Case-fatality rates range from 1 to 10 percent for HFRS and from 25 to 50 percent for HCPS.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The HCPS case-fatality rate does not approach the range given here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Both syndromes are more lethal than this; HFRS alone reaches 10%.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the two rates; HCPS is the more lethal of the two syndromes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A fatality rate of 50-60% is the average for filovirus disease, not for hantavirus infection.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A public health textbook states that 20,000 to 30,000 human cases of hantavirus infection occur worldwide each year. Which of the following best describes the distribution of these infections?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most are New World hantaviruses causing HCPS in the Americas

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most occur in sub-Saharan Africa and cause hepatic failure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nearly all occur in the Four Corners region of the United States

choices.label: D
choices.text: Over 95% are Old World hantaviruses causing HFRS in Asia and Europe

choices.label: E
choices.text: Roughly half cause HCPS and roughly half cause HFRS

explanation.summary: More than 95% of hantavirus infections are Old World viruses causing HFRS in Asia and Europe.
explanation.whyCorrect: There are 20,000-30,000 annual human cases of hantavirus infection worldwide. Most (>95%) are from Old World hantaviruses, cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, and occur in Asia and Europe, while fewer than 500 cases of HCPS occur annually.

whyWrongByChoice.A: New World hantaviruses account for fewer than 500 cases annually, a small fraction of the total.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hantavirus distribution follows rodent reservoir habitats in Asia and Europe, and the syndromes are renal and pulmonary.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The Four Corners outbreak drew attention to HCPS but represents only a small share of global cases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The split is heavily weighted toward HFRS rather than being roughly even.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man cleaned out a rodent-infested cabin 4 days ago and asks how long he should watch for symptoms of hantavirus infection. Which of the following is the typical incubation period from exposure to symptom onset?

explanation.summary: Hantavirus infection has a long incubation period, typically 2 to 3 weeks from exposure to symptoms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hantavirus infection has a long incubation period, typically 2-3 weeks from exposure to symptoms, after which clinical manifestations occur in one of two distinct forms. Monitoring must therefore extend well beyond the first few days.

whyWrongByChoice.A: One to 2 days would be unusually short for hantavirus infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An incubation of hours is far shorter than the described 2- to 3-week period.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The incubation is measured in weeks rather than months.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A year-long incubation is not characteristic of hantavirus infection.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man in South Korea with serologically confirmed hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome becomes oliguric with a creatinine of 6.8 mg/dL and a potassium of 6.5 mEq/L despite fluid resuscitation. In addition to supportive care, which of the following is most likely to be required?

explanation.summary: There is no specific antiviral for hantavirus; HFRS may require dialysis, whereas HCPS may require mechanical ventilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Like filovirus infection, there are no specific antiviral therapies for hantavirus infection, and the cornerstone of therapy is supportive care. Dialysis and mechanical ventilation may be necessary for HFRS and HCPS, respectively, and this patient has severe acute kidney injury with hyperkalemia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No specific antiviral therapy exists for hantavirus infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Corticosteroids are not part of the described management of hantavirus infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mechanical ventilation is the organ support needed in HCPS, where pulmonary edema causes respiratory failure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The approved monoclonal antibody therapies target Ebola virus glycoprotein and are not used for hantavirus.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man in South Korea develops fever, severe back pain, and petechiae 3 weeks after camping in an area with field rodents. Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome is suspected. Which of the following sets of laboratory findings would be most suggestive of this diagnosis?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lymphocytosis, normal platelets, glucosuria, and myoglobinuria

explanation.summary: Leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, elevated creatinine, proteinuria, and hematuria are the laboratory findings suggestive of HFRS.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diagnosis of hantavirus infection rests on a history of potential rodent exposure plus compatible clinical and laboratory findings. Leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, elevated serum creatinine, proteinuria, and hematuria are findings suggestive of HFRS.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Eosinophilia and polycythemia are not features of hantavirus infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thrombocytopenia, not thrombocytosis, is characteristic, and hypercalcemia is unrelated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Platelets fall rather than rise in HFRS, and glucosuria with ketonuria suggests uncontrolled diabetes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The platelet count is typically low, and myoglobinuria points instead to rhabdomyolysis.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A wildlife biologist is surveying animals for hantavirus carriage in several regions of the world. Which of the following groups of animals serves as the reservoir for hantaviruses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chimpanzees, gorillas, and other great apes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deer mice, field mice, rats, shrews, and voles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fruit bats, insectivorous bats, and flying foxes

explanation.summary: Hantavirus reservoirs are all rodents, including deer mice, field mice, rats, shrews, and voles.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hantavirus species and strains display worldwide distributions that correspond to the habitats of their respective reservoirs. Reservoirs are all rodents but include diverse species such as deer mice, field mice, rats, shrews, and voles.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Non-human primates can amplify filovirus transmission but are not hantavirus reservoirs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Domestic mammals are not recognized reservoirs for hantaviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bats are the reservoir for Marburg virus and the likely reservoir for Ebola virus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ticks transmit Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, which is a tick-borne arbovirus.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A cluster of previously healthy adults in the Four Corners region of the southwestern United States, spanning New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, and Colorado, develops a rapidly fatal illness with hypotension and pulmonary edema. This outbreak brought renewed attention to which of the following diseases?

explanation.summary: The Four Corners outbreak of the southwestern United States brought renewed attention to hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hantavirus gained renewed attention with an outbreak of hantavirus (cardio)pulmonary syndrome in the Four Corners region of the southwestern United States, comprising New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, and Colorado. HCPS is caused by New World hantaviruses isolated to the Americas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever is a tick-borne arboviral illness, not a syndrome of the American southwest.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HFRS was recognized during the Korean Conflict of the 1950s and occurs mainly in Asia and Europe.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lassa fever is an arenavirus infection of West Africa.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Marburg virus disease is a bat-associated filovirus infection of Central Africa.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man develops fever, myalgia, and nausea followed within 24 hours by hypotension and severe dyspnea. Chest radiography shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and laboratory studies show thrombocytopenia and leukocytosis with a left shift. Which of the following findings, if present, would be most inconsistent with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome?

explanation.summary: Cough may occur in HCPS, but other features of respiratory tract disease such as rhinorrhea, pharyngitis, and coryza are absent.
explanation.whyCorrect: HCPS features a nonspecific prodrome of fever, myalgia, and nausea followed by rapid onset of hypotension and pulmonary edema caused by capillary leak into the pulmonary bed. Cough may be present, but other features of respiratory tract disease such as rhinorrhea, pharyngitis, and coryza are absent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Rapid onset of hypotension is a defining feature of the syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Leukocytosis with a left shift, along with bilateral interstitial infiltrates, suggests HCPS.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cough may be present in HCPS and does not argue against the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thrombocytopenia is among the laboratory findings that suggest HCPS.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 34-year-old geology student is planning fieldwork in Uganda and asks how to reduce her risk of Marburg virus disease. Which of the following is the most appropriate travel advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid entering caves and mines inhabited by bats

choices.label: B
choices.text: Boil all drinking water and avoid raw vegetables

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive the licensed Marburg virus vaccine before travel

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sleep under a permethrin-treated bed net every night

choices.label: E
choices.text: Take weekly doxycycline prophylaxis before departure

explanation.summary: Travelers to areas of possible filovirus exposure should follow outbreak advisories and avoid caves or mines inhabited by bats.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bats are the reservoir for Marburg virus. If traveling to areas of possible exposure, travelers should follow travel advisories and outbreak alerts issued by health authorities and avoid caves or mines inhabited by bats.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Food and water precautions do not address contact with bats or infected bodily fluids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: There are no approved vaccines for Marburg virus disease; viral vector vaccines exist only for EVD.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bed nets protect against mosquito-borne arboviruses, and filoviruses are not arthropod-borne.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibacterial prophylaxis does not prevent a viral hemorrhagic fever.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A 47-year-old shepherd in Turkey develops fever, myalgias, and widespread ecchymoses one week after removing an engorged tick from his leg. Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever is suspected. The causative agent belongs to which of the following groups of hemorrhagic fever viruses?

explanation.summary: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus is the tick-borne arbovirus among the major agents of viral hemorrhagic fever.
explanation.whyCorrect: The major agents of viral hemorrhagic fever divide into arboviruses and non-arboviruses. Among the arboviruses, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus is the tick-borne agent, in contrast to the mosquito-borne flaviviruses, bunyaviruses, and togaviruses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The bat-borne filoviruses are Ebola and Marburg viruses, which are not arboviruses.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Mosquito-borne flaviviruses include yellow fever, dengue, West Nile, and Zika viruses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lassa fever virus is the rodent-borne arenavirus and is not tick-transmitted.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hantavirus is the rodent-borne bunyavirus, and it is acquired from rodent excreta rather than from ticks.

questions.topicName: Hemorrhagic Viruses

questions.stem: A medical student is reviewing the taxonomy of arboviruses that cause viral hemorrhagic fever. Yellow fever, dengue, and Zika viruses are classified as flaviviruses, whereas Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever and Rift Valley fever viruses are bunyaviruses. Which of the following hemorrhagic-fever arboviruses is classified as a togavirus?

explanation.summary: Chikungunya is the togavirus among the clinically important hemorrhagic-fever arboviruses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clinically relevant arboviruses fall into three families: flaviviruses, togaviruses, and bunyaviruses. Both flaviviruses and togaviruses are enveloped with icosahedral capsids and positive-sense, single-stranded RNA. Chikungunya virus is the togavirus in this group.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dengue virus is a flavivirus, along with yellow fever, West Nile, and Zika.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rift Valley fever virus is a bunyavirus, which has a helical capsid and a segmented, negative-sense RNA genome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yellow fever virus is a flavivirus; the name 'flavi' (yellow) refers to the jaundice it can cause.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zika virus is a flavivirus that is clinically similar to dengue and chikungunya.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman presents with a 2-day history of high-grade fever, headache, and rash. She recently returned from a trip to the Caribbean. On examination she has lymphadenopathy and bilateral hand, wrist, and ankle swelling with marked tenderness and limited range of motion. She reports the joint pain began abruptly and is severe enough to interfere with daily activities. Laboratory tests show normal liver enzymes and a normal platelet count. She denies any bleeding, jaundice, or conjunctivitis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Abrupt, debilitating symmetric polyarthritis of the hands, wrists, and ankles points to chikungunya.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chikungunya is distinguished by inflammatory polyarthritis that is often the first symptom, commonly involves 10 or more joint groups, and characteristically affects the hands, wrists, and ankles. Normal liver enzymes and platelets with no bleeding or jaundice argue against the flaviviruses.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dengue features retro-orbital pain, myalgia, thrombocytopenia, and risk of hemorrhage; disabling joint swelling is not typical.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ebola is not an arbovirus and presents with severe hemorrhagic disease and high mortality, not isolated joint pain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yellow fever is characterized by jaundice, elevated liver enzymes, and mucosal hemorrhage, none of which are present here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zika is usually mild with conjunctivitis and itchy rash and does not cause disabling inflammatory arthritis.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man plans to travel to a region where dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and Zika are all circulating. His physician counsels him that, in addition to mosquito-bite avoidance, he should use condoms and consider abstinence for 2-3 months after returning. For which of the following viruses are these safe-sex practices specifically recommended to reduce person-to-person spread?

explanation.summary: Zika can spread by sexual and vertical (transplacental) transmission, so barrier methods are advised.
explanation.whyCorrect: While Zika is primarily spread by Aedes mosquitoes from the human reservoir, it is also transmitted through sexual contact and across the placenta. The CDC recommends physical barriers or abstinence for 2-3 months after travel to an endemic area.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chikungunya is essentially always transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, not sexually.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dengue is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; sexual transmission is not a recognized route requiring barrier precautions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rift Valley fever spreads via mosquitoes or contact with infected animal fluids, not sexual contact.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yellow fever is mosquito-borne and prevented by vaccination, not safe-sex practices.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A previously healthy traveler returning from South America develops high fever and jaundice, followed within 48 hours by coffee-ground emesis and mucosal bleeding, and dies. At autopsy, liver histology shows scattered small, shrunken, intensely eosinophilic hepatocytes that lack a nucleus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Jaundice, black vomit, and Councilman bodies on liver histology are classic for yellow fever.
explanation.whyCorrect: The eosinophilic, shrunken, anucleate hepatocytes are Councilman (acidophil) bodies, apoptotic hepatocytes seen in yellow fever. The toxic phase of yellow fever produces jaundice with elevated liver enzymes, mucosal hemorrhage, and black ('coffee-ground') vomit.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chikungunya causes inflammatory polyarthritis, not hepatic apoptosis with jaundice and black vomit.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dengue can cause hemorrhage and thrombocytopenia but is not associated with jaundice or Councilman bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rift Valley fever is usually mild; only a small fraction develop hemorrhage, and it is not defined by Councilman bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zika is typically mild in adults and is associated with congenital defects, not fatal hepatic hemorrhagic disease.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman who had a documented dengue infection two years ago while living abroad now develops a second, more severe dengue infection with a different serotype, progressing to hemorrhage and plasma leakage. Which of the following best explains why her second infection is more severe than the first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A bacterial superantigen amplifies the T-cell response

choices.label: B
choices.text: Molecular mimicry triggers autoantibodies against platelets

choices.label: C
choices.text: Non-neutralizing antibodies facilitate viral entry via Fc receptors

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prior infection depleted her complement, preventing viral clearance

choices.label: E
choices.text: The second serotype has a segmented genome allowing reassortment

explanation.summary: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) makes a second dengue infection with a new serotype more severe.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dengue has four serotypes; infection with one gives lifelong immunity to that serotype but not the others. On reinfection with a different serotype, pre-existing non-neutralizing antibodies bind the virus and enhance its entry into monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells via Fc receptors, increasing viral load and disease severity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dengue severity in reinfection is driven by ADE, not by bacterial superantigens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mechanism described is antibody-dependent enhancement of viral entry, not autoantibody-mediated platelet destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ADE increases viral entry through Fc receptors; complement depletion is not the described mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dengue is a flavivirus with a non-segmented, positive-sense RNA genome; reassortment does not apply.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy in the Philippines has had dengue fever for four days. He now develops intense abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, and lethargy, followed by cool extremities, prolonged capillary refill, a feeble pulse, and hypotension. Which of the following complications has he most likely developed?

explanation.summary: Circulatory collapse after dengue warning signs indicates dengue shock syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intense abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, and lethargy are warning signs of impending dengue shock syndrome (DSS). DSS is dengue hemorrhagic fever that leads to circulatory collapse with severe hypotension, prolonged capillary refill, a feeble pulse, and impaired consciousness, and organ failure is possible.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic polyarthritis is a chikungunya complication, not a feature of dengue.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Congenital Zika syndrome affects fetuses/newborns and causes microcephaly, not shock in an older child.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Councilman bodies are apoptotic hepatocytes seen in yellow fever, not a syndrome of circulatory collapse.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Guillain-Barre syndrome is a rare neurologic sequela of Zika, not the cause of hypotensive shock here.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 30-year-old traveler is preparing for a trip to an endemic region of sub-Saharan Africa and is advised to receive vaccination against a mosquito-borne hemorrhagic fever that classically causes jaundice. Which of the following best describes this recommended vaccine?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A live, attenuated yellow fever vaccine

choices.label: C
choices.text: A recombinant virus-like particle chikungunya vaccine

choices.label: D
choices.text: A tick-borne Rift Valley fever vaccine

explanation.summary: Yellow fever, a jaundice-causing mosquito-borne hemorrhagic fever, is prevented with a live, attenuated vaccine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne hemorrhagic fever with notable jaundice that is endemic in parts of Africa and South America. A live, attenuated vaccine is available and recommended for travelers to endemic areas.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The dengue vaccine is live and recombinant, but dengue does not classically cause jaundice and the vaccine is given only to endemic-area residents because of antibody-dependent enhancement.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The chikungunya vaccine is a recombinant virus-like particle product, but chikungunya causes polyarthritis, not jaundice.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rift Valley fever is a bunyavirus with no available vaccine, and it is spread by mosquitoes or animal fluids, not primarily by ticks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There is no vaccine available for Zika.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A woman who was infected with an arbovirus during pregnancy delivers an infant with microcephaly, enlarged cerebral ventricles from cerebrospinal fluid accumulation, intracranial calcifications, and limb contractures. Which of the following viruses is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Microcephaly with ventriculomegaly and brain calcifications defines congenital Zika syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Zika undergoes vertical (transplacental) transmission and can cause congenital Zika syndrome, characterized by microcephaly, brain abnormalities such as ventriculomegaly and calcifications, motor abnormalities including limb contractures and seizures, and eye abnormalities.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chikungunya causes inflammatory polyarthritis and is not a recognized cause of this congenital syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever is a tick-borne bunyavirus causing high-mortality hemorrhagic illness, not congenital defects.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dengue is not associated with congenital microcephaly; it causes hemorrhagic fever and shock.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yellow fever causes jaundice and hepatic hemorrhagic disease, not congenital brain malformations.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 55-year-old shepherd in Central Asia develops sudden fever, headache, jaundice, and joint pain. He recently removed several ticks from his skin. He is hospitalized and his condition is described as carrying roughly a 50% mortality among hospitalized patients. Which of the following is the most likely causative virus, and to which family does it belong?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne togavirus of Asia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus, a bunyavirus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yellow fever virus, a mosquito-borne flavivirus

explanation.summary: Tick exposure in Central Asia with ~50% hospitalized mortality points to Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, a bunyavirus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus is transmitted by Ixodid ticks or the bodily fluids of infected patients, occurs in Central Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, and causes sudden fever, headache, jaundice, and joint pain, with about 50% of hospitalized patients dying. It is a bunyavirus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne togavirus dominated by polyarthritis, not tick transmission with high mortality.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dengue is a mosquito-borne flavivirus and is not spread by ticks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne flavivirus, not a tick-borne illness.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zika is a mosquito-borne flavivirus and does not fit tick exposure with 50% hospitalized mortality.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A public health worker is counseling residents of a region with both mosquito-borne and tick-borne arboviruses on how to reduce their risk of infection. Which of the following measures is most consistent with CDC recommendations for preventing arboviral disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply insect repellent containing DEET or picaridin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete a course of doxycycline before travel

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive post-exposure immunoglobulin after every mosquito bite

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rely solely on a single vaccine that covers all arboviruses

choices.label: E
choices.text: Take prophylactic oral antivirals before outdoor activity

explanation.summary: Vector control and personal protection are the cornerstone of arbovirus prevention.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because a cornerstone of arbovirus prevention is control of the vector, the CDC recommends insect repellents containing DEET or picaridin, clothing treated with permethrin, mosquito netting and screens, eliminating standing water, and removing leaf litter to reduce ticks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxycycline is an antibacterial and does not prevent viral arboviral infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Routine post-exposure immunoglobulin is not a recommended arbovirus prevention strategy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no single vaccine covering all arboviruses; several have no vaccine at all.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No prophylactic antiviral is used to prevent arboviral infection; treatment for most is supportive.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man returns from South America with fever that briefly resolved and then recurred. He now has scleral icterus, laboratory studies showing elevated AST, ALT, and bilirubin, and an episode of coffee-ground emesis. His platelet count is only mildly reduced. Which of the following features best distinguishes his illness from dengue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A human reservoir for the virus

explanation.summary: Prominent jaundice with elevated liver enzymes distinguishes yellow fever from dengue.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is yellow fever, whose toxic phase features jaundice with increased AST, ALT, and bilirubin, mucosal erosion, and black vomit. Marked hepatic involvement with jaundice is a distinguishing feature; dengue is characterized more by retro-orbital pain, myalgia, and thrombocytopenia rather than jaundice.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both viruses use humans as a reservoir, so this feature is shared rather than distinguishing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Retro-orbital pain is characteristic of dengue, so it would not distinguish this illness from dengue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Severe thrombocytopenia is a hallmark of dengue hemorrhagic fever, not a distinguishing feature of yellow fever.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Both yellow fever and dengue are transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, so this does not separate them.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 26-year-old backpacker returns from Southeast Asia with the sudden onset of a fever of 40 C (104 F), a rash, severe pain behind the eyes, and such intense muscle and bone pain that he can barely move. A CBC shows neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: High fever with retro-orbital pain and 'breakbone' myalgia plus neutropenia and thrombocytopenia is classic dengue.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dengue fever presents with high fever plus two or more of rash, neutropenia, retro-orbital pain, arthralgia, headache, and myalgia. The myalgia can be so severe that dengue is called 'breakbone fever,' and CBCs typically show neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Southeast Asia is a hyper-endemic region.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chikungunya is dominated by debilitating inflammatory polyarthritis, not retro-orbital pain with neutropenia and thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rift Valley fever occurs in eastern and southern Africa and is usually mild, not a Southeast Asian breakbone-fever illness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Yellow fever prominently causes jaundice and elevated liver enzymes, which are absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zika is usually mild with conjunctivitis and itchy rash, without severe breakbone myalgia and marked cytopenias.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is bitten by a mosquito carrying an arbovirus and develops a brief febrile illness. Testing shows that his blood never reaches a viral level high enough to infect mosquitoes that later feed on him, so transmission is not sustained through people like him. Which of the following terms best describes his role in the arbovirus life cycle?

explanation.summary: A host that cannot pass the virus back to a vector is a dead-end (incidental) host.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the arbovirus life cycle, a vector feeding on a host introduces virus into the bloodstream, where it amplifies to levels that cause viremia; that viremia is what allows another feeding vector to acquire the virus. A host that does not sustain transmissible viremia is called a dead-end, or incidental, host.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A host in which the virus amplifies to transmissible levels continues the cycle, which is the opposite of what happened here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The vector is the arthropod that carries and transmits the virus, not the infected person.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hosts that sustain viremia and can pass virus back to feeding vectors are reservoirs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vectors are arthropods such as mosquitoes and ticks, not human patients.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A laboratory characterizes the virus isolated from a patient with Rift Valley fever and compares it with a dengue virus isolate from another patient. Which of the following best describes the structure and genome of the Rift Valley fever isolate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enveloped, helical capsid, circular segmented negative-sense single-stranded RNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enveloped, helical capsid, linear positive-sense single-stranded RNA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enveloped, icosahedral capsid, linear positive-sense single-stranded RNA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nonenveloped, helical capsid, linear negative-sense single-stranded RNA

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nonenveloped, icosahedral capsid, circular segmented negative-sense single-stranded RNA

explanation.summary: Bunyaviruses such as Rift Valley fever virus are enveloped with helical capsids and circular, segmented, negative-sense RNA genomes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rift Valley fever virus is a bunyavirus. Bunyaviruses are enveloped and typically have helical capsids, and their negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genomes are circular and segmented. This contrasts with dengue, a flavivirus, whose genome is linear and positive-sense.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Bunyavirus genomes are negative-sense and segmented, not linear and positive-sense.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This describes the flaviviruses and togaviruses, including the dengue isolate used for comparison.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bunyaviruses are enveloped, and their genomes are circular and segmented rather than linear.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bunyaviruses are enveloped, not nonenveloped, although the genome description is correct.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 40-year-old logger develops yellow fever after several weeks of work in a forested region of South America where non-human primates also carry the virus. Which of the following best characterizes this form of yellow fever compared with the urban form?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Transmitted by Aedes aegypti, with humans as the sole reservoir in urban outbreaks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transmitted by Aedes aegypti, with non-human primates as the only reservoir in forested areas

choices.label: C
choices.text: Transmitted by Haemogogus mosquitoes, and the more common of the two epidemiologic forms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transmitted by Haemogogus mosquitoes, with humans and non-human primates as reservoirs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transmitted by Ixodid ticks, with livestock and wild mammals as the reservoir

explanation.summary: Jungle yellow fever is spread by Haemogogus mosquitoes, and both humans and non-human primates can serve as the reservoir.
explanation.whyCorrect: Yellow fever is divided into urban and jungle forms based on the region of likely acquisition. Jungle yellow fever, acquired in forested areas, is transmitted by Haemogogus mosquitoes, and the reservoir can be both humans and non-human primates. It is of much less clinical importance than the urban form.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This describes urban yellow fever, which is transmitted by Aedes aegypti from the human reservoir.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aedes aegypti transmits the urban form, and the jungle reservoir includes humans as well as non-human primates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Haemogogus transmission is correct for jungle yellow fever, but the urban form is the more common one.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ixodid tick transmission with an animal link describes Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, not yellow fever.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man with yellow fever recovers from an initial febrile illness, but within 48 hours he becomes jaundiced, bleeds from the gums, and produces black vomit. Approximately what proportion of patients who enter this phase die, and over what interval?

explanation.summary: Roughly half of patients who enter the toxic phase of yellow fever die within 7 to 10 days.
explanation.whyCorrect: Yellow fever has an initial phase lasting 3 to 4 days, after which most patients recover. Less than 48 hours after that apparent recovery, 10% to 15% of patients develop the toxic phase of intoxication, and roughly half of those who enter the toxic phase die within 7 to 10 days.

whyWrongByChoice.A: About 1% is the overall mortality of Rift Valley fever, not of the yellow fever toxic phase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 10% to 15% is the proportion of patients who enter the toxic phase, not the proportion who die once in it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Toxic-phase mortality is substantially higher than 25%, and death occurs within 7 to 10 days.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mortality in the toxic phase is roughly half, not near-universal.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A febrile traveler returning from an endemic region of Africa has suspected yellow fever. Which of the following is the gold standard laboratory test for confirming the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blood culture on selective bacterial media

choices.label: B
choices.text: Liver biopsy with hematoxylin and eosin staining

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peripheral blood smear for intraerythrocytic parasites

choices.label: D
choices.text: Real-time reverse transcriptase PCR of blood or serum

explanation.summary: Real-time RT-PCR (RT-qPCR) of blood or serum is the gold standard for diagnosing yellow fever.
explanation.whyCorrect: The gold standard for laboratory diagnosis of yellow fever is real-time reverse transcriptase PCR of blood or serum. Rapid PCR or ELISA detection of IgM to viral antigens may also be used to make the diagnosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Yellow fever is a viral infection; bacterial blood cultures will not detect it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Liver biopsy during illness is avoided, and Councilman bodies are typically a postmortem histologic finding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Intraerythrocytic parasites on smear point to malaria, a different febrile illness of the same regions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bilirubin and aminotransferases document hepatic injury but do not identify the virus.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with jaundice and suspected yellow fever is being evaluated. A trainee proposes an urgent percutaneous liver biopsy to look for Councilman bodies. Which of the following is the best reason to avoid this procedure during the acute illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Biopsy tissue cannot be processed histologically during viremia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Councilman bodies appear only after antiviral therapy is started

choices.label: C
choices.text: The liver is not involved during the toxic phase

choices.label: D
choices.text: The procedure carries a high risk of hemorrhage

explanation.summary: Liver biopsy is withheld during acute yellow fever because of the bleeding risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Yellow fever produces mucosal erosion and hemorrhage, so liver biopsy during illness should not be performed because of the risk of hemorrhage. Councilman bodies, the apoptotic hepatocytes characteristic of yellow fever, are instead described on postmortem histology, while diagnosis in life relies on RT-qPCR or serology.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tissue can be processed normally; the problem is the hazard of obtaining it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Councilman bodies are apoptotic hepatocytes produced by the infection itself, not by treatment; no specific antiviral exists.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The liver is prominently involved, with jaundice and elevated AST, ALT, and bilirubin during the toxic phase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibody-dependent enhancement is an immunologic phenomenon of dengue reinfection, unrelated to biopsy.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 28-year-old traveler is admitted with yellow fever complicated by jaundice and mucosal bleeding. Which of the following best describes the treatment of his infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A live, attenuated vaccine administered at the time of diagnosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: A targeted antiviral agent directed against the viral polymerase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aggressive supportive care, because no specific antiviral is available

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exchange transfusion to clear apoptotic hepatocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glucocorticoids combined with disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs

explanation.summary: Yellow fever is treated with aggressive supportive care; there is no specific antiviral therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment of yellow fever consists of aggressive supportive care, as no specific antiviral therapy is available. Prevention, rather than treatment, is where the live attenuated vaccine acts.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The live, attenuated yellow fever vaccine is preventive and is given before exposure, not as treatment of established disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No specific antiviral therapy for yellow fever is available.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Councilman bodies are dying hepatocytes within the liver and cannot be removed from the circulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glucocorticoids and DMARDs are used for the chronic joint pain that follows chikungunya.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A global health lecture notes that roughly 100,000 severe cases of yellow fever occur worldwide each year. Approximately how many deaths from yellow fever occur worldwide each year?

explanation.summary: Yellow fever causes roughly 100,000 severe cases and 40,000 deaths worldwide each year.
explanation.whyCorrect: Each year, roughly 100,000 severe cases and 40,000 deaths occur from yellow fever worldwide. Dengue, by comparison, is more prevalent but less deadly, with about 400 million cases and 20,000 deaths per year.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Roughly 200 deaths were reported worldwide from chikungunya in 2024.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This figure does not correspond to the burden of any of the arboviruses discussed.
whyWrongByChoice.C: About 20,000 deaths per year are attributed to dengue, not yellow fever.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 400 million is the approximate number of dengue cases per year, not yellow fever deaths.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: An infection control team is classifying the major agents of viral hemorrhagic fever by how they reach humans. Which of the following agents is a bunyavirus that spreads from rodents rather than through an arthropod vector?

explanation.summary: Hantavirus is a rodent-borne bunyavirus and therefore is not an arbovirus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the major agents of viral hemorrhagic fever, the arboviruses are the mosquito-borne and tick-borne agents. Hantavirus is grouped with the rodent viruses that are not arboviruses, yet it is a bunyavirus, the same family as Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever and Rift Valley fever viruses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus is a bunyavirus, but it is tick-borne and therefore an arbovirus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lassa fever virus is spread by rodents but is an arenavirus, not a bunyavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Marburg virus is a bat-associated filovirus, not a rodent-borne bunyavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rift Valley fever virus is a bunyavirus, but it is mosquito-borne and therefore an arbovirus.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 10-year-old boy in Southeast Asia has had fever for 5 days. He now has petechiae and purpura over the legs and a right-sided pleural effusion. Laboratory studies show a platelet count of 28,000/mm3 and hypoproteinemia. His blood pressure is normal, his pulse is full, and capillary refill is brisk. Which of the following best classifies his illness?

explanation.summary: Fever for 2 to 7 days with hemorrhage, plasma leakage, and severe thrombocytopenia, but no circulatory collapse, defines dengue hemorrhagic fever.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dengue hemorrhagic fever displays fever of 2 to 7 days, hemorrhage, plasma leakage, and severe thrombocytopenia. The vascular changes may produce petechiae, purpura, pleural effusion, or hypoproteinemia, all present in this boy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemorrhagic manifestations are rare in chikungunya, which is dominated by inflammatory polyarthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dengue fever is high fever plus features such as rash, neutropenia, retro-orbital pain, arthralgia, headache, and myalgia, without plasma leakage and severe thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dengue shock syndrome requires circulatory collapse with severe hypotension, prolonged capillary refill, and a feeble pulse, none of which he has.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Yellow fever's toxic phase features jaundice with elevated liver enzymes and black vomit rather than plasma leakage with effusion.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A resident of a dengue-endemic country receives the dengue vaccine, which is a live, recombinant product. Which of the following best describes how this vaccine is constructed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inactivated whole virions from all four dengue serotypes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Live, attenuated dengue virus of a single circulating serotype

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recombinant virus-like particles assembled from dengue envelope protein

choices.label: D
choices.text: The dengue virus genome with inserted yellow fever envelope and pre-membrane genes

choices.label: E
choices.text: The yellow fever virus genome with inserted dengue envelope and pre-membrane genes

explanation.summary: The dengue vaccine is a yellow fever virus backbone carrying dengue envelope and pre-membrane genes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The dengue vaccine is live and recombinant: it consists of the yellow fever virus genome with inserted genes from the four strains of dengue virus, including the genes for envelope and pre-membrane proteins. Because of antibody-dependent enhancement, it is given only to people who live in an endemic area.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The vaccine is live rather than an inactivated whole-virion preparation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The vaccine incorporates genes from all four dengue strains rather than one attenuated serotype.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A recombinant virus-like particle vaccine is the chikungunya product, not the dengue vaccine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The backbone is the yellow fever virus genome, with dengue genes inserted into it, not the reverse.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl with dengue hemorrhagic fever has developed plasma leakage with a falling blood pressure and prolonged capillary refill. Which of the following is the mainstay of her treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An antiviral agent directed against the flavivirus polymerase

choices.label: C
choices.text: High-dose glucocorticoids to reduce vascular permeability

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediate administration of the live recombinant dengue vaccine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intravenous fluids and blood products to maintain intravascular volume

explanation.summary: Severe dengue is treated by aggressively maintaining intravascular volume and pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment for dengue consists predominantly of maintaining intravascular volume and pressure. Supportive care is aggressive and may include intravenous fluids, whole blood, or packed red blood cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No targeted antiviral therapy is available for dengue; treatment of viral hemorrhagic fever is supportive.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dengue is viral, so antibacterial therapy does not address the plasma leakage or thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucocorticoids are used for chronic chikungunya joint pain, not for dengue plasma leakage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The dengue vaccine is preventive and is restricted to residents of endemic areas; it has no role in treating active disease.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: In antibody-dependent enhancement of dengue, non-neutralizing or sub-neutralizing antibodies bind virions and facilitate their entry into host cells through Fc receptors, increasing viral replication. Which of the following cell types are the principal targets of this enhanced entry?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CD4+ T lymphocytes and plasma cells

explanation.summary: Antibody-dependent enhancement drives dengue virus into Fc-receptor-bearing monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: In antibody-dependent enhancement, pre-existing antibody from an earlier infection with a different serotype binds the new virus, and the antibody-virus complex is taken up through Fc gamma receptors on monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells. The result is increased viral load and more severe disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lymphocytes and plasma cells are not the Fc-receptor-bearing phagocytic targets described in this phenomenon.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Thrombocytopenia occurs in severe dengue, but red cells and megakaryocytes are not the Fc-receptor-bearing targets of enhanced entry.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatocyte apoptosis with Councilman bodies is a feature of yellow fever, not the target of dengue antibody-dependent enhancement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasma leakage reflects vascular change in severe dengue, but endothelial cells are not the cells into which enhanced entry occurs.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman had confirmed chikungunya 8 months ago and still has swollen, painful wrists and ankles. She asks how common her ongoing arthritis is after this infection. Chronic polyarthritis is reported in approximately what proportion of people with past chikungunya infection?

explanation.summary: Chronic polyarthritis follows chikungunya in 40% to 70% of previously infected people.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic polyarthritis is reported in 40% to 70% of people with past chikungunya infection, and in roughly 60% of those it persists beyond 18 months. This debilitating arthritis is the feature that gave the disease its name, from a Makonde verb meaning 'to assume a contorted position.'

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chronic arthritis after chikungunya is far more common than a few percent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 10% to 15% is the proportion of yellow fever patients who enter the toxic phase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This underestimates the frequency of post-chikungunya chronic polyarthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chronic polyarthritis is common but does not affect nearly all previously infected people.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has had disabling symmetric hand and wrist arthritis for 2 years following a documented chikungunya infection. Scheduled acetaminophen no longer controls her symptoms, and her joints remain swollen with prolonged morning stiffness. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Administer the recombinant chikungunya vaccine to clear the infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug such as methotrexate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Start an antiviral agent directed against the togavirus

explanation.summary: Chronic chikungunya joint pain is treated with glucocorticoids, DMARDs, or neuropathic pain agents.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acute chikungunya is treated supportively with agents such as acetaminophen, but chronic joint pain may be treated with glucocorticoids, disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, or even medications for neuropathic pain such as gabapentin. Patients with chronic inflammatory arthritis from chikungunya can improve markedly on methotrexate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The chikungunya vaccine is preventive and is aimed at travelers to areas with active outbreaks, not at treating established arthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chikungunya is a viral illness, and antibacterial therapy has no role in its arthritis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Her symptoms are disabling and no longer controlled by acetaminophen, so escalation of therapy is warranted.
whyWrongByChoice.E: No targeted antiviral therapy exists for chikungunya.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man returning from a chikungunya outbreak has had 2 days of high fever, rash, and severe joint pain. He is hemodynamically stable with a normal platelet count. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for his acute illness?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intravenous fluids and packed red blood cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Supportive care with acetaminophen for pain

explanation.summary: Acute chikungunya is treated supportively, with symptom-targeted agents such as acetaminophen.
