explanation.whyCorrect: For acute chikungunya disease, treatment is supportive and targeted to symptoms, for example acetaminophen for pain. Drugs such as glucocorticoids, DMARDs, or gabapentin are reserved for chronic joint pain that persists after the acute illness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neuraminidase inhibitors act on influenza virus and have no activity against a togavirus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aggressive volume and blood-product support is the approach to severe dengue, and he has no plasma leakage or thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunoglobulin is not part of the supportive management of acute chikungunya.
whyWrongByChoice.D: DMARDs such as methotrexate are used for chronic post-chikungunya arthritis, not for a 2-day acute illness.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man hospitalized with acute chikungunya develops chest pain, an elevated troponin level, and new global left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography. Which of the following best characterizes this finding?

explanation.summary: Myocarditis is among the rare severe complications of acute chikungunya infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Severe complications of chikungunya are rare but may include respiratory failure, myocarditis, acute hepatitis, kidney failure, hemorrhage, and neurologic involvement. Troponin elevation with new ventricular dysfunction during acute infection fits myocarditis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Limb contractures are motor abnormalities of congenital Zika syndrome, not a complication in adults.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Councilman bodies are the apoptotic hepatocytes seen in yellow fever.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dengue shock syndrome is circulatory collapse complicating dengue hemorrhagic fever, not a cardiac complication of chikungunya.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Microcephaly is a manifestation of congenital Zika syndrome in an infected fetus.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A public health agency reports that dengue and chikungunya are now appearing in areas where they were previously absent. Which of the following best explains this change in distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibody-dependent enhancement of infection in previously exposed residents

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased rates of sexual transmission among returning travelers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reassortment between segmented viral genomes during coinfection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Urbanization, deforestation, and climate change expanding vector habitats

choices.label: E
choices.text: Waning immunity from prior yellow fever vaccination in endemic areas

explanation.summary: Arbovirus distribution tracks vector habitat, which urbanization, deforestation, and climate change can expand.
explanation.whyCorrect: The distribution of arboviral infections closely correlates with the distribution of their vectors, and environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, rainfall, and standing water affect vector breeding and survival. Urbanization, deforestation, and climate change can expand vector habitats and thereby increase the geographic range of arboviral infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibody-dependent enhancement increases the severity of a second dengue infection; it does not move the disease into new territory.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sexual transmission is a recognized route for Zika but does not account for the spread of mosquito-borne dengue and chikungunya into new regions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dengue and chikungunya have non-segmented genomes, so reassortment does not apply.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Yellow fever vaccination protects against yellow fever and has no bearing on where dengue and chikungunya occur.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is planning travel to a country currently experiencing an active chikungunya outbreak. In addition to mosquito-bite avoidance, which of the following preventive measures is specifically indicated for this infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Physical barriers or abstinence for 2 to 3 months

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prophylactic scheduled acetaminophen during the trip

choices.label: C
choices.text: The live, attenuated yellow fever vaccine

explanation.summary: A recombinant virus-like particle chikungunya vaccine is recommended for travelers to areas with an active outbreak.
explanation.whyCorrect: A recombinant, viral-like particle vaccine for chikungunya received FDA approval in 2025 and is recommended for travelers to areas with an active chikungunya outbreak.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Barrier methods and abstinence after travel are advised for Zika, which can spread sexually; chikungunya is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acetaminophen treats symptoms of acute disease and does not prevent infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The live, attenuated yellow fever vaccine protects against yellow fever, not chikungunya.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Because of antibody-dependent enhancement, the dengue vaccine is given only to people who live in an endemic area, and it does not cover chikungunya.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A physician is counseling a group of adult travelers about Zika virus. Which of the following best describes the usual course of Zika virus infection in older children and adults?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accompanied by severe hemorrhage and shock

choices.label: B
choices.text: Asymptomatic in roughly 80% of those infected

choices.label: C
choices.text: Characterized by jaundice and black vomit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fatal in most cases without supportive care

explanation.summary: Zika is typically asymptomatic in about 80% of infected older children and adults.
explanation.whyCorrect: Zika virus infection in older children and adults is typically asymptomatic, in roughly 80% of cases, or causes mild disease. The 20% of cases that are symptomatic often present with conjunctivitis, low-grade fever, and an itchy rash.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hemorrhage with circulatory collapse is characteristic of severe dengue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Jaundice and black vomit describe the toxic phase of yellow fever.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Disabling inflammatory polyarthritis is the hallmark of chikungunya.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zika is usually mild; the high case-fatality arbovirus discussed is yellow fever.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: Three weeks after a mild febrile illness with conjunctivitis and an itchy rash acquired while traveling in Brazil, a 34-year-old man develops progressive symmetric weakness that began in his legs and has ascended, with absent deep tendon reflexes. Which of the following complications has he most likely developed?

explanation.summary: Ascending areflexic weakness after a Zika-like illness reflects Guillain-Barre syndrome, a rare neurologic sequela.
explanation.whyCorrect: His mild illness with conjunctivitis and itchy rash is typical of symptomatic Zika. Rarely, Zika infection results in severe thrombocytopenia or neurological sequelae such as Guillain-Barre syndrome and transverse myelitis; ascending symmetric weakness with areflexia is the classic picture of the former.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute hepatitis is a rare severe complication of chikungunya and would present with liver dysfunction rather than weakness.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic inflammatory polyarthritis follows chikungunya and causes joint swelling and stiffness, not areflexic weakness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Congenital Zika syndrome affects a fetus exposed in utero, not an infected adult.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dengue shock syndrome is circulatory collapse during acute dengue, not a delayed neurologic syndrome.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman who is 12 weeks pregnant acquired Zika virus infection while traveling. In addition to congenital malformations in the fetus, she is at increased risk for which of the following adverse outcomes?

explanation.summary: Zika infection in pregnancy increases the risk of preterm birth, miscarriage, and stillbirth in addition to congenital Zika syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infection during pregnancy can cause severe adverse outcomes: increased risk of preterm birth, fetal death (miscarriage) and stillbirth, and congenital malformations referred to as congenital Zika syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gestational diabetes is not among the described adverse outcomes of Zika infection in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Inflammatory polyarthritis is a feature of chikungunya rather than Zika.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Jaundice with hepatic failure characterizes the toxic phase of yellow fever, not maternal Zika infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zika is associated with an increased risk of preterm birth, the opposite of post-term delivery.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 31-year-old traveler returns from a region where dengue, chikungunya, and Zika all circulate. He has a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis. He has no joint swelling or morning stiffness, no retro-orbital pain, and a normal platelet count. Which of the following features is most useful in distinguishing his infection from dengue and chikungunya?

explanation.summary: Conjunctivitis is prominent in Zika and is the feature that best separates it from dengue and chikungunya.
explanation.whyCorrect: Symptomatic Zika typically presents with conjunctivitis, low-grade fever, and an itchy rash. Conjunctivitis is not a feature of dengue and is at most minor in chikungunya, so it is the most discriminating finding among the overlapping presentations of these three infections.

whyWrongByChoice.B: All three infections cause fever, so it cannot separate them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Headache is common to dengue, chikungunya, and Zika alike.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Myalgia is shared by all three and is most prominent in dengue, but it does not identify Zika.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rash occurs in all three infections and is therefore not discriminating.

questions.topicName: Arboviruses

questions.stem: A 45-year-old livestock worker in eastern Africa develops fever, weakness, back pain, and dizziness several days after assisting with the delivery of calves during a large outbreak of abortions in the herd. He also sustained numerous mosquito bites. He has no jaundice or bleeding and recovers uneventfully over a week. Which of the following is the most likely infection?

explanation.summary: A mild febrile illness in an eastern African livestock worker exposed to animal fluids and mosquitoes is Rift Valley fever.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rift Valley fever virus is transmitted by mosquitoes or by the bodily fluids of infected animals and is found in eastern and southern Africa, where infection of livestock is common. Affected people often have no symptoms or a mild illness that includes fever, weakness, back pain, and dizziness; fewer than 1% develop mucosal erosion and hemorrhage, jaundice, and bloody vomit or stool.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chikungunya would be dominated by abrupt, debilitating polyarthritis of the hands, wrists, and ankles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever follows Ixodid tick exposure in Central Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, with sudden fever, headache, jaundice, and joint pain and 50% mortality among hospitalized patients.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dengue causes high fever with retro-orbital pain, severe myalgia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia, and it is not acquired from animal fluids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Yellow fever would be expected to produce jaundice with elevated liver enzymes and mucosal hemorrhage in its toxic phase.
